sentences.zh: 【唐紀五十九】起昭陽單閼，盡著雍涒灘，凡六年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records, Part 59] Beginning with the year Zhaoyang-danyan and ending with Zhu-yong-tuantan, altogether six years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records, Part 59] Spanning six years, from the Zhaoyang-danyan cycle year through Zhu-yong-tuantan.

sentences.zh: 穆宗睿聖文惠孝皇帝下長慶三年（

translations.literal: Below [the annals of] Emperor Muzong, the Sagely, Cultured, Gracious, and Filial — the third year of Changqing (
translations.idiomatic: In the lower annals of Emperor Muzong, the Sagely, Cultured, Gracious, and Filial Emperor, the third year of Changqing (

sentences.zh: 癸卯，公元八二三年）

translations.literal: guimao, corresponding to AD 823)
translations.idiomatic: guimao, AD 823)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸未，賜兩軍中尉以下錢。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the day guiwei, [the emperor] bestowed money on the two Armies' eunuch-commanders and all below them.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month's guiwei day, the emperor distributed cash gifts to the eunuch-commanders of the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies and their subordinates.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛卯，賜統軍、軍使等綿彩、銀器各有差。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day xinmao, [the emperor] bestowed silk brocade and silver vessels on army commanders, military commissioners, and the like, each in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the xinmao day, he granted silk brocade and silver vessels to army commanders and military commissioners in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎牛僧孺，素為上所厚。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Niu Sengru had long been treated with favor by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Niu Sengru had long enjoyed the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 初，韓弘之子右驍衛將軍公武為其父謀，以財結中外。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han Hong's son, Right Brave Guards General Gongwu, had schemed on his father's behalf, using wealth to win over people inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han Hong's son Gongwu, a general of the Right Brave Guards, had worked on his father's behalf, using money to cultivate allies at court and beyond.

sentences.zh: 及公武卒，弘繼薨，稚孫紹宗嗣，主藏奴與吏訟於御史府。

translations.literal: When Gongwu died, Hong soon followed in death; the young grandson Shaozong succeeded [the estate], and the chief steward slave brought suit against officials at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: After Gongwu died and Hong soon followed, the young grandson Shaozong inherited the estate, and the chief steward brought a lawsuit against officials at the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 上憐之，盡取弘財簿自閱視，凡中外主權，多納弘貨，獨朱句細字曰：「某年月日，送戶部牛侍郎錢千萬，不納。

translations.literal: The emperor took pity on him, took Hong's entire account books and read through them himself; of all those in and outside the court who held power, most had accepted Hong's goods — only one entry in red ink in fine characters read: 'On such-and-such year, month, and day, sent ten million cash to Vice Minister Niu of the Revenue Ministry; not accepted.'
translations.idiomatic: Taking pity on the family, the emperor personally went through Hong's account books. Nearly every powerful figure at court and beyond had taken Hong's money — except one line in fine red ink: 'On [date], sent ten million cash to Vice Minister Niu of Revenue; declined.'

sentences.zh: 」上大喜，以示左右曰：「果然，吾不繆知人！

translations.literal: [The emperor] was greatly pleased and showed it to those beside him, saying: 'It is true — I do not misjudge men!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and showed those around him, saying, 'Just as I thought — I do not misjudge men!'

sentences.zh: 」三月，壬戌，以僧孺為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day renxu, Sengru was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the renxu day, Sengru was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 時僧孺與李德裕皆有入相之望。

translations.literal: At that time both Sengru and Li Deyu had hopes of entering the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: At the time both Sengru and Li Deyu had been expected to reach the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 德裕出為浙西觀察使，八年不遷。

translations.literal: Deyu had been sent out as military governor of Zhexi and for eight years received no promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu had been posted as governor of Zhexi and had gone eight years without promotion.

sentences.zh: 以為李逢吉排己，引僧孺為相，由是牛、李之怨愈深。

translations.literal: [Deyu] believed that Li Fengji had excluded him and brought Sengru in as chief minister; from this the enmity between the Niu and Li factions grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Li Fengji had blocked him and installed Sengru as chief minister, Deyu deepened the rift between the Niu and Li factions.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲午，安南奏陸州獠攻掠州縣。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day jiawu, Annan reported that Liao tribesmen of Luzhou were attacking and plundering prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the fourth month's jiawu day, Annan reported that Liao tribesmen in Luzhou were raiding prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 丙申，賜宣徽院供奉官錢，紫衣者百二十緡，下至承旨各有差。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, [the emperor] bestowed money on the attendants of the Xuanhui Court: those in purple robes received one hundred and twenty strings, and down to the chief secretaries each received differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day he granted cash to the Xuanhui Court attendants — one hundred and twenty strings for those in purple robes, with lesser amounts down to the chief secretaries.

sentences.zh: 初，翼城人鄭注，眇小，目下視，而巧譎傾諂，善揣人意，以醫游四方，羈貧甚。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zheng Zhu of Yicheng was slight in stature, with downcast eyes, yet crafty, deceitful, and fawning; skilled at reading people's minds, he wandered the four quarters practicing medicine and was extremely poor and destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zheng Zhu of Yicheng was a slight man with downcast eyes, but crafty, deceitful, and ingratiating, skilled at reading people's wishes. He wandered as a physician and lived in bitter poverty.

sentences.zh: 嘗以藥術干徐州牙將，牙將悅之，薦於節度使李愬。

translations.literal: Once he presented his medical arts to a guard officer of Xuzhou; the officer was pleased and recommended him to Military Governor Li Su.
translations.idiomatic: He once offered his medical skills to a guard officer in Xuzhou; pleased, the officer recommended him to Military Governor Li Su.

sentences.zh: 愬餌其藥頗驗，遂有寵，署為牙推，浸預軍政，妄作威福，軍府患之。

translations.literal: Su took his medicines with considerable effect, and Zhu soon won favor; he was appointed military adjutant, gradually took part in military administration, arrogantly wielded power for private gain, and the headquarters was troubled by him.
translations.idiomatic: Su found his medicines effective and soon favored him, appointing him military adjutant. Zhu gradually intruded into military affairs, abused his power, and the headquarters grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 監軍王守澄以眾情白愬，請去之，愬曰：「注雖如是，然奇才也，將軍試與之語，苟無可取，去之未晚。

translations.literal: Supervising Commissioner Wang Shoucheng reported the general sentiment to Su and asked that Zhu be removed. Su said: 'Although Zhu is like this, he is nevertheless a rare talent. General, try speaking with him; if there is nothing to be gained from him, removing him will not be too late.'
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Commissioner Wang Shoucheng reported the men's discontent and asked Su to dismiss Zhu. Su replied, 'Zhu may be like this, but he is a rare talent. Try talking with him; if he proves worthless, you can remove him later.'

sentences.zh: 」乃使注往謁守澄，守澄初有難色，不得已見之。

translations.literal: He then had Zhu go to call on Shoucheng. Shoucheng at first showed reluctance but, having no choice, received him.
translations.idiomatic: Su sent Zhu to call on Shoucheng, who at first showed reluctance but finally received him.

sentences.zh: 坐語未久，守澄大喜，延之中堂，促膝笑語，恨相見之晚。

translations.literal: They had not been seated and talking long when Shoucheng was greatly delighted, invited him into the central hall, sat knee to knee laughing and talking, and regretted that they had met so late.
translations.idiomatic: They had scarcely begun to talk when Shoucheng was delighted, brought him into the central hall, and sat knee to knee in easy conversation, lamenting that they had met so late.

sentences.zh: 明日，謂愬曰：「鄭生誠如公言。

translations.literal: The next day he said to Su: 'Master Zheng is indeed as you said.'
translations.idiomatic: The next day he told Su, 'Master Zheng is indeed as you said.'

sentences.zh: 」自是又有寵於守澄，權勢益張，愬署為巡官，列於賓席。

translations.literal: From then on Zhu again enjoyed favor with Shoucheng; his power grew ever greater, and Su appointed him touring officer, ranking him among the guests of honor.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Zhu won Shoucheng's favor as well, and his power grew. Su appointed him touring officer and seated him among honored guests.

sentences.zh: 注既用事，恐牙將薦己者洩其本末，密以它愬，愬殺之。

translations.literal: Once Zhu was in power, he feared that the guard officer who had recommended him would reveal his origins; he secretly accused the man on other grounds, and Su had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power, Zhu feared the guard officer who had recommended him would expose his past. He secretly denounced the man on other grounds, and Su had him killed.

sentences.zh: 及守澄入知樞密，挈注以西，為立居宅，贍給之。

translations.literal: When Shoucheng entered [the capital] to serve in the Bureau of Military Affairs, he took Zhu west with him, built him a residence, and supported him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shoucheng entered the capital to serve in the Bureau of Military Affairs, he brought Zhu west, built him a house, and provided for him.

sentences.zh: 遂薦於上，上亦厚遇之。

translations.literal: He then recommended Zhu to the emperor, and the emperor also treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended Zhu to the emperor, who also treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 自上有疾，守澄專制國事，勢傾中外。

translations.literal: From the time the emperor fell ill, Shoucheng monopolized state affairs, and his power overshadowed court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor fell ill, Shoucheng monopolized state affairs, and his power overshadowed the entire court.

sentences.zh: 注日夜出入其家，與之謀議，語必通夕，關通賂遺，人莫能突擊其跡。

translations.literal: Zhu went in and out of his house day and night, deliberating with him; their talk always lasted until dawn; he handled bribes and gifts, and no one could break through to trace his tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu came and went from his house day and night, plotting with him until dawn, handling bribes and gifts so deftly that no one could trace his dealings.

sentences.zh: 始則有微賤巧宦之士，或因以求進，數年之後，達官車馬滿其門矣。

translations.literal: At first there were only low-born, clever office-seekers who used him to seek advancement; after several years, high officials' carriages and horses filled his gate.
translations.idiomatic: At first only humble, ambitious men used him to seek promotion; within a few years the carriages of high officials crowded his gate.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書鄭權，家多姬妾，祿薄不能贍，因注通於守澄以求節鎮。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zheng Quan had many concubines at home; his salary was thin and could not support them, so through Zhu he connected with Shoucheng to seek a frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zheng Quan kept many concubines but could not support them on his salary, so he used Zhu to reach Shoucheng and seek a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以權為嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, Quan was appointed military governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day Quan was appointed military governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬申，以尚書左丞柳公綽為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day renshen, Senior Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Liu Gongchuo was appointed military governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the renshen day, Senior Assistant Director Liu Gongchuo was appointed military governor of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 公綽過鄧縣，有二吏，一犯贓，一舞文，眾謂公綽必殺犯贓者。

translations.literal: Passing through Deng County, Gongchuo found two clerks — one guilty of embezzlement, one of twisting the law — and the crowd said Gongchuo would surely kill the embezzler.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Deng County, Gongchuo found two clerks, one guilty of embezzlement and one of twisting the law. People assumed he would execute the embezzler.

sentences.zh: 公綽判曰：「贓吏犯法，法在；

translations.literal: Gongchuo judged: 'The corrupt clerk violated the law — the law remains;
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo ruled, 'The corrupt clerk broke the law, but the law remains;

sentences.zh: 奸吏亂法，法亡。

translations.literal: the treacherous clerk disrupted the law — the law is destroyed.'
translations.idiomatic: the treacherous clerk subverted the law, and the law is destroyed.'

sentences.zh: 」竟誅舞文者。

translations.literal: In the end he executed the one who had twisted the law.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he executed the one who had twisted the law.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以晉、慈二州為保義軍，以觀察使李寰為節度使。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, the two prefectures of Jin and Ci were constituted as the Baoyi Army, and Observation Commissioner Li Huan was made its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day the prefectures of Jin and Ci were organized as the Baoyi Army, with Observation Commissioner Li Huan as military governor.

sentences.zh: 六月，己丑，以吏部侍郎韓愈為京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jichou, Vice Minister of Personnel Han Yu was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the jichou day, Vice Minister of Personnel Han Yu was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 六軍不敢犯法，私相謂曰：「是尚欲燒佛骨，何可犯也！

translations.literal: The Six Armies did not dare break the law; they said to one another in private: 'This is a man who was ready to burn Buddhist relics — how could we offend him!'
translations.idiomatic: The Six Armies dared not break the law and whispered among themselves, 'This is the man who wanted to burn Buddhist relics — how could we cross him!'

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸亥，嶺南奏黃洞蠻寇邕州，破左江鎮。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day guihai, Lingnan reported that Huangdong barbarians raided Yongzhou and broke Zuo River garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the seventh month's guihai day, Lingnan reported that Huangdong tribesmen raided Yongzhou and overran Zuo River garrison.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，邕州奏黃洞蠻破欽州千金鎮，刺史楊嶼奔石南砦。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, Yongzhou reported that Huangdong barbarians had broken Qianjin garrison in Qinzhou; Prefect Yang Yu fled to Shinan stockade.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day Yongzhou reported that Huangdong tribesmen had overrun Qianjin garrison in Qinzhou and that Prefect Yang Yu had fled to Shinan stockade.

sentences.zh: 南詔勸利卒，國人請立其弟豐祐。

translations.literal: Quanli of Nanzhao died, and the people of the state asked that his younger brother Fengyou be established [as king].
translations.idiomatic: Quanli of Nanzhao died, and his subjects asked that his younger brother Fengyou be enthroned.

sentences.zh: 豐祐勇敢，善用其眾，始慕中國，不與父連名。

translations.literal: Fengyou was brave and skilled in employing his forces; he began to admire China and did not link his name with his father's.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyou was brave and skilled at leading his men; he began to admire China and did not include his father's name in his own.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸已，邕管奏破黃洞蠻。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day guisi, Yong Circuit reported defeating the Huangdong barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the guisi day, Yong Circuit reported a victory over the Huangdong tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 丙申，上自復道幸興慶宮，至通化門樓，投絹二百匹施山僧。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, the emperor went by the covered passageway to Xingqing Palace; reaching Tonghua Gate tower, he cast two hundred bolts of silk as alms to mountain monks.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day the emperor traveled by the covered passageway to Xingqing Palace and, at Tonghua Gate tower, tossed two hundred bolts of silk as alms to mountain monks.

sentences.zh: 上之濫賜皆此類，不可悉記。

translations.literal: The emperor's indiscriminate gifts were all of this sort and cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's lavish gifts were all of this kind and cannot all be recorded.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以左僕射裴度為司空、山南西道節度使，不兼平章事。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, Left Vice Director Pei Du was appointed Minister of Works and military governor of Shannan West Circuit, without retaining the concurrent title of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day Left Vice Director Pei Du was made Minister of Works and military governor of Shannan West Circuit, without retaining his chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 李逢吉惡度，右補闕張又新等附逢吉，競流謗毀傷度，竟出之。

translations.literal: Li Fengji hated Du; Right Remonstrator Zhang Youxin and others attached themselves to Fengji and vied in spreading slander to injure Du, until Du was finally sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji hated Du; Right Remonstrator Zhang Youxin and others attached themselves to Fengji and competed in slandering him until Du was finally sent out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 又新，薦之子也。

translations.literal: Youxin was the son of [Zhang] Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Youxin was the son of Zhang Jian.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙辰，加昭義節度使劉悟同平章事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day bingchen, Zhaoyi Military Governor Liu Wu was given the additional title of Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the bingchen day, Zhaoyi Military Governor Liu Wu was made Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 李逢吉為相，內結知樞密王守澄，勢傾朝野。

translations.literal: Li Fengji served as chief minister, bonded inwardly with Bureau Director Wang Shoucheng, and his power overshadowed court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Li Fengji allied with Bureau Director Wang Shoucheng, and his power overshadowed the court.

sentences.zh: 惟翰林學士李紳每承顧問，常排抑之，擬狀至內庭，紳多所臧否。

translations.literal: Only Hanlin Academician Li Shen, whenever consulted, regularly checked and restrained him; when draft memorials reached the inner court, Shen often approved or rejected them.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hanlin Academician Li Shen, whom the emperor often consulted, regularly checked him; when draft memorials reached the inner court, Shen often approved or rejected them.

sentences.zh: 逢吉患之，而上待遇方厚，不能遠也。

translations.literal: Fengji was troubled by this, but the emperor's treatment of Shen was then still generous, and he could not remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji resented this, but the emperor still favored Shen and Fengji could not remove him.

sentences.zh: 會御史中丞缺，逢吉薦紳清直，宜居風憲之地。

translations.literal: When the post of Censor-in-Chief fell vacant, Fengji recommended Shen as upright and pure, fit to occupy the post of wind and law.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of Censor-in-Chief fell vacant, Fengji recommended Shen as upright and fit for the censorate.

sentences.zh: 上以中丞亦次對官，不疑而可之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the censor-in-chief was also an official who answered in turn at audience, approved without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Because the censor-in-chief also answered at imperial audiences, the emperor approved without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 會紳與京兆尹兼御史大夫韓愈爭台參及它職事，文移往來，辭語不遜。

translations.literal: Just then Shen and Metropolitan Governor and Concurrent Censor Grandee Han Yu disputed attendance at the censorate and other duties; documents went back and forth in language that was not respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Shen and Metropolitan Governor and Concurrent Censor Grandee Han Yu quarreled over censorate protocol and other duties, exchanging documents in disrespectful language.

sentences.zh: 逢吉奏二人不協，冬，十月，丙戌，以愈為兵部侍郎，紳為江西觀察使。

translations.literal: Fengji memorialized that the two were not in harmony; in winter, in the tenth month, on the day bingxu, Yu was made Vice Minister of War and Shen military governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji reported that the two were at odds; in winter, on the tenth month's bingxu day, Yu was made Vice Minister of War and Shen governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以中書侍郎、同平章事杜元穎同平章事，充西川節度使。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister Du Yuanying was appointed Associate Chief Minister and military governor of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day Vice Director Du Yuanying was appointed Associate Chief Minister and military governor of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，安南奏黃洞蠻為寇。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Annan reported that Huangdong barbarians were raiding.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day Annan reported Huangdong tribesmen on the march.

sentences.zh: 韓愈、李紳入謝，上各令自敘其事，乃深寤。

translations.literal: Han Yu and Li Shen came in to give thanks for their appointments; the emperor had each narrate the affair in his own words, and then deeply understood.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu and Li Shen came to give thanks for their appointments; the emperor had each explain the dispute in his own words and then fully understood.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，復以愈為吏部侍郎，紳為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Yu was again made Vice Minister of Personnel and Shen Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day Yu was restored as Vice Minister of Personnel and Shen as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 穆宗睿聖文惠孝皇帝下長慶四年（

translations.literal: Below [the annals of] Emperor Muzong, the Sagely, Cultured, Gracious, and Filial — the fourth year of Changqing (
translations.idiomatic: In the lower annals of Emperor Muzong, the Sagely, Cultured, Gracious, and Filial Emperor, the fourth year of Changqing (

sentences.zh: 甲辰，公元八二四年）

translations.literal: jiachen, corresponding to AD 824)
translations.idiomatic: jiachen, AD 824)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛亥朔，上始御含元殿朝會。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the first day xinhai, the emperor for the first time held court audience in Hanyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month's xinhai new-moon day, the emperor held his first court audience in Hanyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 初，柳泌等既誅，方士稍復，因左右以進，上餌其金石之藥。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Liu Bi and the others had been executed, Daoist adepts gradually returned; through those close to the emperor they were introduced, and the emperor took their mineral and metal medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Liu Bi and others were executed, Daoist adepts gradually returned; introduced through the emperor's intimates, he began taking their mineral elixirs.

sentences.zh: 有處士張皋者上疏，以為：「神慮淡則血氣和，嗜欲勝則疾疹作。

translations.literal: A recluse named Zhang Gao submitted a memorial, stating: 'When the spirit's thoughts are tranquil, blood and breath are harmonious; when desires prevail, illness arises.'
translations.idiomatic: A recluse named Zhang Gao submitted a memorial arguing that when the mind is calm the body is in harmony, but when desires prevail illness follows.

sentences.zh: 藥以攻疾，無疾不可餌也。

translations.literal: 'Medicine is for attacking illness; without illness one must not take it.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Medicine is meant to fight disease; without disease one must not take it.'

sentences.zh: 昔孫思邈有言：『藥勢有所偏助，令人藏氣不平，借使有疾用藥，猶須重慎。

translations.literal: Formerly Sun Simiao said: 'The potency of medicine has partial effects; it makes the stored breaths within a person unbalanced — even if there is illness and medicine is used, one must still be greatly cautious.'
translations.idiomatic: Sun Simiao once said, 'Medicine's potency is partial and disturbs the body's balance; even when treating illness one must be extremely cautious.'

sentences.zh: 』庶人尚爾，況於天子！

translations.literal: 'Even commoners are so — how much more the Son of Heaven!'
translations.idiomatic: 'If commoners must be so careful, how much more the Son of Heaven!'

sentences.zh: 先帝信方士妄言，餌藥致疾，此陛下所詳知也，豈得復循其覆轍乎！

translations.literal: The late emperor believed the reckless words of adepts, took medicine, and brought on illness — this Your Majesty knows in detail; how can you again follow in their overturned tracks!'
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor believed adepts' reckless talk, took their elixirs, and fell ill — Your Majesty knows this well. How can you repeat the same mistake!'

sentences.zh: 今朝野之人紛紜竊議，但畏忤旨，莫敢進言。

translations.literal: Now people at court and in the countryside whisper in discussion, but fearing to go against the imperial will, none dare speak forth.
translations.idiomatic: Now court and countryside whisper about this, but fearing to offend the throne, none dare speak openly.

sentences.zh: 臣生長蓬艾，麋鹿與游，無所邀求，但粗知忠義，欲裨萬一耳！

translations.literal: Your servant grew up among weeds and mugwort, consorting with deer — with nothing to seek, knowing only in rough fashion loyalty and righteousness, wishing to be of the slightest benefit, that is all!'
translations.idiomatic: I grew up among weeds, keeping company with deer, seeking nothing for myself — knowing only loyalty and wishing to serve in the smallest way!'

sentences.zh: 」上甚善其言，使求之，不獲。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly approved his words and had him sought, but he could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly approved his words and had him sought, but he could not be found.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，嶺南奏黃洞蠻寇欽州，殺將吏。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, Lingnan reported that Huangdong barbarians raided Qinzhou and killed officers.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day Lingnan reported that Huangdong tribesmen raided Qinzhou and killed officers.

sentences.zh: 庚午，上疾復作。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, the emperor's illness recurred.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day the emperor's illness returned.

sentences.zh: 壬申，大漸，命太子監國。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, [his condition] grew critical; he ordered the crown prince to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day his condition grew critical, and he ordered the crown prince to oversee the state.

sentences.zh: 宦官欲請郭太后臨朝稱制。

translations.literal: The eunuchs wished to ask Empress Dowager Guo to attend court and rule as regent.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs wished to have Empress Dowager Guo attend court as regent.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「昔武後稱制，幾傾社稷。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: 'In former times Empress Wu ruled as regent and nearly overturned the altars of state.'
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, 'When Empress Wu ruled as regent she nearly overturned the dynasty.'

sentences.zh: 我家世守忠義，非武氏之比也。

translations.literal: 'Our family for generations has kept loyalty and righteousness — we are not to be compared with the Wu clan.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Our family has kept faith with the throne for generations — we are not the Wu clan.'

sentences.zh: 太子雖少，但得賢宰相輔之，卿輩勿預朝政，何患國家不安！

translations.literal: 'Although the crown prince is young, if only worthy chief ministers assist him, and you do not interfere in court politics — what worry is there that the state will not be secure!'
translations.idiomatic: 'The crown prince is young, but with worthy chief ministers to assist him, and if you stay out of court politics, what danger can there be to the realm!'

sentences.zh: 自古豈有女子為天下主，而能致唐、虞之理乎！

translations.literal: 'Since antiquity has there ever been a woman as ruler of all under Heaven who could bring about the governance of Tang and Yu!'
translations.idiomatic: 'Since antiquity has any woman ruled the realm and brought about the golden age of Yao and Shun!'

sentences.zh: 」取制書手裂之。

translations.literal: She took the draft edict and tore it apart with her hands.
translations.idiomatic: She took the draft edict and tore it apart.

sentences.zh: 太后兄太常卿釗聞有是議，密上箋曰：「若果徇其請，臣請先帥諸子納官爵歸田裡。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's elder brother, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhao, hearing that there was such a proposal, secretly submitted a memorial saying: 'If they truly carry out this request, your servant asks first to lead my sons in surrendering our offices and ranks and returning to the countryside.'
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the proposal, the empress dowager's elder brother Zhao, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, secretly submitted a memorial: 'If this is granted, I ask first to lead my sons in resigning our offices and returning to the countryside.'

sentences.zh: 」太后泣曰：「祖考之慶，鐘於吾兄。

translations.literal: The empress dowager wept and said: 'The blessings of our ancestors have gathered upon my brother.'
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wept and said, 'Our ancestors' blessing rests on my brother.'

sentences.zh: 」是夕，上崩於寢殿。

translations.literal: That evening the emperor died in the sleeping hall.
translations.idiomatic: That evening the emperor died in his sleeping hall.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以李逢吉攝塚宰。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, Li Fengji was appointed acting chief of mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day Li Fengji was appointed acting chief mourner.

sentences.zh: 丙子，敬宗即位於太極東序。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Emperor Jingzong ascended the throne in the eastern wing of Taiji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day Emperor Jingzong ascended the throne in the eastern wing of Taiji Hall.

sentences.zh: 初，穆宗之立，神策軍士人賜錢五十千，宰相議以太厚難繼，乃下詔稱：「宿衛之勒，誠宜厚賞，屬頻年旱歉，御府空虛，邊兵尚未給儀，沾恤期於均濟。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Muzong was established [as heir], each man of the Divine Strategy Army was granted fifty thousand cash; the chief ministers discussed that this was too generous to continue, and an edict was issued stating: 'The toil of the palace guard truly deserves generous reward, but successive years of drought and poor harvest have emptied the imperial treasury; frontier troops have not yet been provided their stipends — the extension of favor must await equal relief.'
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong was enthroned, each Divine Strategy soldier had been granted fifty thousand cash. The chief ministers judged the amount unsustainable, and an edict declared that while the palace guard deserved generous reward, years of drought had emptied the treasury and frontier troops still lacked pay, so relief must be shared equally.

sentences.zh: 神策軍士人賜絹十匹、錢十千，畿內諸鎮又減五千。

translations.literal: Each man of the Divine Strategy Army was granted ten bolts of silk and ten thousand cash; the garrisons within the capital region had a further reduction of five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Each Divine Strategy soldier received ten bolts of silk and ten thousand cash, while garrisons in the capital region had five thousand more cut.

sentences.zh: 仍出內庫綾二百萬匹付度支，充邊軍春衣。

translations.literal: Two million bolts of damask from the inner treasury were also issued to the Revenue Ministry to serve as spring clothing for frontier troops.
translations.idiomatic: Two million bolts of damask from the inner treasury were also issued to Revenue to supply frontier troops with spring clothing.

sentences.zh: 」時人善之。

translations.literal: People of the time approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time praised the decision.

sentences.zh: 自戊寅至庚辰，上賜宦官服色及錦彩金銀甚眾，或今日賜綠，明日賜緋。

translations.literal: From the day wuyin to gengchen, the emperor bestowed on eunuchs rank robes and brocade, gold, and silver in great quantity; some received green today and crimson tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: From wuyin through gengchen the emperor lavished rank robes, brocade, gold, and silver on eunuchs — some receiving green one day and crimson the next.

sentences.zh: 初，穆宗既留李紳，李逢吉愈忌之。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Muzong had kept Li Shen in office, Li Fengji hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: After Muzong had kept Li Shen in office, Li Fengji hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 紳族子虞頗以文學知名，自言不樂仕進，隱居華陽川，及從父耆為左拾遺，虞與耆書求薦，誤達於紳。

translations.literal: Shen's clansman Yu was fairly renowned for literary accomplishment; he said himself that he took no joy in pursuing office and lived in seclusion on Huayang Stream. When his father's younger cousin Qi became Left Reminder, Yu wrote Qi seeking recommendation, but the letter mistakenly reached Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's kinsman Yu was known for his literary talent and claimed to shun office, living in seclusion on Huayang Stream. When Yu's cousin Qi became Left Reminder, Yu wrote Qi asking for recommendation, but the letter mistakenly reached Shen.

sentences.zh: 紳以書誚之，且以語於眾人。

translations.literal: Shen wrote back to mock him and also spoke of it to the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Shen wrote back to mock him and told the story publicly.

sentences.zh: 虞深怨之，乃詣逢吉，悉以紳平日密論逢吉之語告之。

translations.literal: Yu deeply resented this; he then went to Fengji and fully reported to him Shen's private remarks about Fengji on ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: Yu deeply resented this and went to Fengji, reporting everything Shen had privately said against him.

sentences.zh: 逢吉益怒，使虞與補闕張又新及從子前河陽掌書記仲言等伺求紳短，揚之於士大夫間。

translations.literal: Fengji grew still angrier and had Yu, together with Remonstrator Zhang Youxin and his nephew Zhongyan, formerly secretary at Heyang, and others, seek out Shen's faults and spread them among the scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji grew angrier still and set Yu, Remonstrator Zhang Youxin, and his nephew Zhongyan, formerly secretary at Heyang, to hunt for Shen's faults and spread them among officials.

sentences.zh: 且言「紳潛察士大夫有群居議論者，輒指為朋黨，白之於上。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Shen secretly watches scholar-officials who gather in groups to discuss affairs and invariably denounces them as faction members, reporting them to the emperor.'
translations.idiomatic: He also claimed that Shen secretly watched officials who met in groups to discuss affairs, denounced them as faction members, and reported them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 」由是士大夫多忌之。

translations.literal: From this scholar-officials mostly feared and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: From this many officials came to fear and resent Shen.

sentences.zh: 及敬宗即位，逢吉與其黨快紳失勢，又恐上復用之，日夜謀議，思所以害紳者。

translations.literal: When Jingzong ascended the throne, Fengji and his faction rejoiced at Shen's loss of power, yet also feared the emperor might use him again; day and night they plotted, seeking means to harm Shen.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong ascended the throne, Fengji and his faction rejoiced at Shen's fall but feared the emperor might restore him; day and night they plotted how to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 楚州刺史蘇遇謂逢吉之黨曰：「主上初聽政，必開延英，有次對官，惟此可防。

translations.literal: Chuzhou Prefect Su Yu said to Fengji's faction: 'When the sovereign first attends to government, he is sure to open Yanying Hall; there are officials who answer in turn — only this can be guarded against.'
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou Prefect Su Yu told Fengji's followers, 'When the emperor first takes up government he will hold audience in Yanying Hall with officials who answer in turn — that is our only opening.'

sentences.zh: 」其黨以為然，亟白逢吉曰：「事迫矣，若俟聽政，悔不可追！

translations.literal: His faction thought this correct and urgently reported to Fengji: 'The matter is urgent; if we wait until he holds audience, regret cannot be undone!'
translations.idiomatic: They agreed and urgently told Fengji, 'Time is running out; if we wait until he holds audience, it will be too late!'

sentences.zh: 」逢吉乃令王守澄言於上曰：「陛下所以為儲貳，臣備知之，皆逢吉之力也。

translations.literal: Fengji then had Wang Shoucheng speak to the emperor, saying: 'The reason Your Majesty became heir apparent — your servant knows it in full — was entirely through Fengji's power.'
translations.idiomatic: Fengji had Wang Shoucheng tell the emperor, 'Your Majesty owes your position as heir entirely to Fengji's efforts.'

sentences.zh: 如杜元穎、李紳輩，皆欲立深王。

translations.literal: Men like Du Yuanying and Li Shen all wished to establish Prince Shen as heir.'
translations.idiomatic: Men like Du Yuanying and Li Shen all wanted to make Prince Shen heir.'

sentences.zh: 」度支員外郎李續之等繼上章言之。

translations.literal: Revenue Ministry Assistant Director Li Xuzhi and others followed with memorials stating the same.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Ministry Assistant Director Li Xuzhi and others followed with memorials saying the same.

sentences.zh: 上時年十六，疑未信。

translations.literal: The emperor was then sixteen years old and doubted, not yet believing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was only sixteen and remained doubtful.

sentences.zh: 會逢吉亦有奏，言「紳謀不利於上，請加貶謫。

translations.literal: Just then Fengji also submitted a memorial, saying: 'Shen plotted against the emperor's advantage; please add further demotion and exile.'
translations.idiomatic: Then Fengji himself memorialized that Shen had plotted against the emperor and asked for a harsher exile.

sentences.zh: 」上猶再三覆問，然後從之。

translations.literal: The emperor still questioned repeatedly before consenting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned the matter repeatedly before finally consenting.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸未，貶紳為端州司馬。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day guiwei, Shen was demoted to army adjutant of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the guiwei day, Shen was demoted to army adjutant of Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 逢吉仍帥百官表賀，既退，百官復詣中書賀，逢吉方與張又新語，門者弗內。

translations.literal: Fengji still led the hundred officials in a congratulatory memorial; after they withdrew, the hundred officials again went to the Secretariat to congratulate, but Fengji was just then speaking with Zhang Youxin and the gatekeeper would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji led the officials in a congratulatory memorial, and when they came to the Secretariat afterward to congratulate again, Fengji was talking with Zhang Youxin and the gatekeeper refused them entry.

sentences.zh: 良久，又新揮汗而出，旅揖百官曰：「端溪之事，又新不敢多讓。

translations.literal: After a long while Youxin came out waving off sweat and bowed to the officials in file, saying: 'In the affair of Duan Creek, Youxin dares not yield much credit to others.'
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Youxin emerged wiping his brow and bowed to the officials, saying, 'In the Duan Creek affair I dare not yield much credit to others.'

sentences.zh: 」眾駭愕辟易，憚之。

translations.literal: The crowd was startled and drew back in alarm, fearing him.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd recoiled in shock and fear.

sentences.zh: 右拾遺內供奉吳思獨不賀，逢吉怒，以思為吐蕃告哀使。

translations.literal: Right Reminder and Inner Attendant Wu Si alone did not congratulate; Fengji was angry and appointed Si envoy to Tibet to announce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Right Reminder Wu Si alone refused to congratulate; Fengji in anger sent him as envoy to Tibet to announce mourning.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，貶翰林學士龐嚴為信州刺史，蔣防為汀州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, Hanlin Academician Pang Yan was demoted to prefect of Xinzhou and Jiang Fang to prefect of Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day Hanlin Academicians Pang Yan and Jiang Fang were demoted to prefects of Xinzhou and Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 嚴，壽州人。

translations.literal: Yan was a man of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was from Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 與防皆紳所引也。

translations.literal: Both he and Fang had been introduced by Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Both had been promoted by Shen.

sentences.zh: 給事中於敖，素與嚴善，封還敕書。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yu Ao had long been on good terms with Yan and returned the sealed edict unopened.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Yu Ao, who was close to Yan, returned the edict unopened.

sentences.zh: 人為之懼。

translations.literal: People were afraid for him.
translations.idiomatic: People feared for him.

sentences.zh: 曰：「於給事為龐、蔣直冤，犯宰相怒，誠所難也！

translations.literal: They said: 'Supervising Secretary Yu spoke up for Pang and Jiang's injustice — to offend the chief minister's anger is truly difficult!'
translations.idiomatic: They said, 'Yu spoke up for Pang and Jiang — to defy the chief minister takes real courage!'

sentences.zh: 」及奏下，乃言貶之太輕，逢吉由是獎之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was issued, he said the demotion was too light, and Fengji therefore rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued he said the demotion was too light, and Fengji rewarded him for it.

sentences.zh: 張又新等猶忌紳，日上書言貶紳太輕，上許為殺之。

translations.literal: Zhang Youxin and others still resented Shen; day by day they submitted memorials saying Shen's demotion was too light, and the emperor agreed to have him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Youxin and others still hated Shen and daily memorialized that his punishment was too light; the emperor agreed to have him killed.

sentences.zh: 朝臣莫敢言，獨翰林侍讀學士韋處厚上疏，指述「紳為逢吉之黨所讒，人情歎駭。

translations.literal: Court officials dared not speak; only Hanlin Attendant Reader Wei Chuhou submitted a memorial, stating plainly: 'Shen has been slandered by Fengji's faction; public sentiment sighs in shock.'
translations.idiomatic: No court official dared speak; only Hanlin Attendant Reader Wei Chuhou submitted a memorial stating that Shen had been slandered by Fengji's faction and that the public was appalled.

sentences.zh: 紳蒙先朝獎用，借使有罪，猶宜容假，以成三年無改之孝，況無罪乎！

translations.literal: Shen received the late emperor's commendation and employment; even if he had guilt, he should still be granted forbearance to fulfill the three years' filial piety without change — how much more when he is without guilt!'
translations.idiomatic: Shen had been honored by the late emperor; even if guilty he deserved forbearance to fulfill mourning filial piety — how much more when he was innocent!'

sentences.zh: 」於是上稍開寤，會閱禁中文書，有穆宗所封一篋，發之，得裴度、杜元穎、李紳疏請立上為太子，上乃嗟歎，悉焚人所上譖紳書。

translations.literal: The emperor then slightly awakened; happening to review palace documents, there was a casket sealed by Muzong; opening it, he found memorials by Pei Du, Du Yuanying, and Li Shen requesting that he be established as crown prince. The emperor sighed and burned all the memorials slandering Shen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor began to understand. Reviewing palace documents he found a casket sealed by Muzong; inside were memorials from Pei Du, Du Yuanying, and Li Shen supporting his appointment as heir. He sighed and burned every memorial slandering Shen.

sentences.zh: 雖未即召還，後有言者，不復聽矣。

translations.literal: Although Shen was not immediately recalled, afterward when anyone spoke [against him], the emperor no longer listened.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shen was not immediately recalled, the emperor would hear no further accusations against him.

sentences.zh: 己亥，尊郭太后為太皇太后。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, Empress Dowager Guo was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day Empress Dowager Guo was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 乙已，尊上母王妃為皇太后。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, the emperor's mother, Lady Wang, was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day the emperor's mother, Lady Wang, was honored as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后，越州人也。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was a native of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was from Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 丁未，上幸中和殿擊球，自是數游宴、擊球、奏樂，賞賜宦官、樂人，不可悉紀。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, the emperor visited Zhonghe Hall to play ball; from then on he repeatedly went on pleasure outings, played ball, and had music performed, bestowing rewards on eunuchs and musicians beyond full record.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day the emperor went to Zhonghe Hall to play cuju. Thereafter he constantly feasted, played ball, and enjoyed music, lavishing rewards on eunuchs and musicians beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬子，赦天下。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day renzi, a general amnesty was declared throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the renzi day, a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 諸道常貢之外，毋得進奉。

translations.literal: Beyond the regular tribute from each circuit, no additional presentations were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond regular tribute from each circuit, no additional presentations were permitted.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，上始對宰相於延英殿。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, the emperor for the first time answered chief ministers in Yanying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day the emperor held his first audience with chief ministers in Yanying Hall.

sentences.zh: 初，牛元翼在襄陽，數賂王庭水奏以清其家，庭湊不與。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Niu Yuanji was at Xiangyang, he repeatedly bribed Wang Tingcou to memorialize clearing his family; Tingcou would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Niu Yuanji was at Xiangyang, he repeatedly bribed Wang Tingcou to petition clearing his family, but Tingcou refused.

sentences.zh: 聞元翼薨，甲子，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Hearing that Yuanji had died, on the day jiazi he killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned Yuanji had died, on the jiazi day he slaughtered the entire family.

sentences.zh: 上視朝每晏，戊辰，日絕高尚未坐，百官班於紫宸門外，老病者幾至僵踣。

translations.literal: The emperor was late for court audience every day; on the day wuchen the sun was already high and he had not yet taken his seat; the hundred officials stood in formation outside Zichen Gate, and the old and sick nearly collapsed from stiffness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was habitually late for court. On the wuchen day the sun stood high and he still had not appeared; officials waited outside Zichen Gate until the old and sick nearly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫李渤白宰相曰：「昨日疏論坐晚，今晨愈甚，請出閣待罪於金吾仗。

translations.literal: Remonstrating Censor Li Bo told the chief ministers: 'Yesterday I memorialized on the lateness of audience; this morning it is worse. I ask to leave the hall and await punishment at the Golden Crow guard post.'
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating Censor Li Bo told the chief ministers, 'Yesterday I protested the late audience; today it is worse. I ask leave to await punishment at the Golden Crow guard post.'

sentences.zh: 」既坐班退，左拾遺劉栖楚獨留，進言曰：「憲宗及先帝皆長君，四方猶多叛亂。

translations.literal: After the formation was seated and withdrew, Left Reminder Liu Qichu alone remained and advanced, saying: 'Emperors Xianzong and the late emperor were both mature rulers, yet the four quarters still had many rebellions.'
translations.idiomatic: After the officials withdrew, Left Reminder Liu Qichu alone remained and said, 'Emperors Xianzong and your father were mature rulers, yet rebellions still plagued the realm.'

sentences.zh: 陛下富於春秋，嗣位之初，當宵衣求理。

translations.literal: 'Your Majesty is rich in youth; at the beginning of succession you should rise at midnight to seek good government.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Your Majesty is young; at the start of your reign you should rise before dawn to govern.'

sentences.zh: 而嗜寢樂色，日晏方起，梓宮在殯，鼓吹日喧，令聞未彰，惡聲遐布。

translations.literal: 'Yet you love sleep and delight in beauty, rising only when the day is late; the imperial coffin still lies in mourning while music blares daily — good repute is not yet displayed, and evil report spreads far.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Yet you love sleep and pleasure, rising only late in the day while your father's coffin still lies in state and music blares daily. Good repute has not appeared, but ill report spreads far.'

sentences.zh: 臣恐福祚之不長，請碎首王階以謝諫職之曠。

translations.literal: 'Your servant fears your blessings and tenure will not be long; I ask to dash my head on the imperial steps to atone for neglect of remonstrance duty.'
translations.idiomatic: 'I fear your reign will not be long; let me dash my head on the palace steps to atone for failing in my duty as remonstrator.'

sentences.zh: 」遂以額叩龍墀，見血不已，響聞閤外。

translations.literal: He then struck his forehead on the imperial dais until blood flowed without cease, the sound heard outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then struck his forehead on the imperial dais until blood flowed, the sound heard outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 李逢吉宣曰：「劉栖楚休叩頭，俟進止！

translations.literal: Li Fengji announced: 'Liu Qichu, cease knocking your head; await the emperor's decision!'
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji announced, 'Liu Qichu, stop — await the emperor's decision!'

sentences.zh: 」栖楚捧首而起，更論宦官事，上連揮令出。

translations.literal: Qichu rose holding his head and spoke further on the matter of eunuchs; the emperor repeatedly waved him to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Qichu rose holding his head and spoke further about the eunuchs; the emperor repeatedly waved him out.

sentences.zh: 栖楚曰：「不用臣言，請繼以死。

translations.literal: Qichu said: 'If you do not use my words, I ask to follow them with death.'
translations.idiomatic: Qichu said, 'If you will not heed me, let me die here.'

sentences.zh: 」牛僧孺宣曰：「所奏知，門外俟進止！

translations.literal: Niu Sengru announced: 'Your memorial is noted; wait outside for the decision!'
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru announced, 'Your memorial is noted; wait outside for the decision!'

sentences.zh: 」栖楚乃出，待罪金吾仗，於是宰相贊成其言。

translations.literal: Qichu then went out and awaited punishment at the Golden Crow guard post; the chief ministers thereupon endorsed his words.
translations.idiomatic: Qichu withdrew to await punishment at the Golden Crow guard post, and the chief ministers endorsed his words.

sentences.zh: 上命中使就仗，並李渤宣慰令歸。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered palace envoys to the guard post to comfort both men and command their return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent palace envoys to comfort both men and order them home.

sentences.zh: 尋擢栖楚為起居舍人，仍賜緋。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Qichu was promoted to Diarist and also granted crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qichu was promoted to diarist and granted crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 栖楚辭疾不拜，歸東都。

translations.literal: Qichu declined on grounds of illness and did not accept the appointment, returning to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Qichu declined on grounds of illness and returned to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 庚午，賜內教坊錢萬緡，以備行幸。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, ten thousand strings of cash were granted to the Inner Music Office to prepare for imperial excursions.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day ten thousand strings of cash were granted to the Inner Music Office for imperial excursions.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲午，淮南節度使王播罷鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day jiawu, Huainan Military Governor Wang Bo was removed as salt and iron transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the fourth month's jiawu day, Huainan Military Governor Wang Bo was removed as salt and iron transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以布衣姜洽為補闕，試大理評事陸洿、布衣李虞、劉堅為拾遺。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, commoner Jiang Qia was made Remonstrator; probationary Grand Court Assessor Lu Yu and commoners Li Yu and Liu Jian were made Reminders.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day commoner Jiang Qia was made remonstrator, probationary court assessor Lu Yu and commoners Li Yu and Liu Jian were made removers.

sentences.zh: 時李逢吉用事，所親厚者張又新、李仲言、李續之、李虞、劉栖楚、姜洽及拾遺張權輿、程昔范，又有從而附麗之者，時人惡逢吉者，目之為八關、十六子。

translations.literal: At that time Li Fengji held power; those he favored were Zhang Youxin, Li Zhongyan, Li Xuzhi, Li Yu, Liu Qichu, Jiang Qia, and Reminders Zhang Quanyu and Cheng Xifan, with others who attached themselves — those who hated Fengji called them the Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji then held power. His favorites included Zhang Youxin, Li Zhongyan, Li Xuzhi, Li Yu, Liu Qichu, Jiang Qia, and removers Zhang Quanyu and Cheng Xifan, with many hangers-on. His enemies called them the Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons.

sentences.zh: 卜者蘇玄明與染坊供人張韶善，玄明謂韶曰：「我為子卜，當升殿坐，與我共食。

translations.literal: Diviner Su Xuanming was on good terms with Zhang Shao, a dyeworks laborer; Xuanming said to Shao: 'I have divined for you — you will ascend the hall and sit, and eat with me.'
translations.idiomatic: Diviner Su Xuanming was close to Zhang Shao, a dyeworks laborer. Xuanming told him, 'I have divined for you — you will ascend the hall and sit, and we will eat together.'

sentences.zh: 今主上晝夜球、獵，多不在宮中，大事可圖也。

translations.literal: 'Now the sovereign day and night plays ball and hunts and is often not in the palace — a great affair can be plotted.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The emperor spends day and night playing ball and hunting and is often away from the palace — a great deed can be attempted.'

sentences.zh: 」韶以為然，乃與玄明謀結染工無賴者百餘人，丙申，匿兵於紫草，車載以入銀台門，伺夜作亂。

translations.literal: Shao thought this right; he and Xuanming plotted to gather more than a hundred ruffians among the dyeworkers. On the day bingshen they hid weapons in purple-dyed goods, loaded them on carts, and entered through Yintai Gate, waiting for night to raise a disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Shao agreed. He and Xuanming gathered more than a hundred ruffians from the dyeworks. On the bingshen day they hid weapons in bundles of purple-dyed goods, carted them through Yintai Gate, and waited for night to strike.

sentences.zh: 未達所詣，有疑其重載而詰之者，韶急，即殺詰者，與其徒易服揮兵，大呼趣禁庭。

translations.literal: Before they reached their destination, someone suspicious of the heavy load questioned them; Shao in haste killed the questioner, he and his followers changed clothes and brandished weapons, shouting as they rushed toward the forbidden court.
translations.idiomatic: Before they reached their goal someone questioned the heavy load. Shao killed him, changed clothes with his men, brandished weapons, and shouted as they rushed the palace.

sentences.zh: 上時在清思殿擊球，諸宦者見之，驚駭，急入閉門，走白上。

translations.literal: The emperor was then playing ball in Qingsi Hall; the eunuchs who saw them were startled, hurried in to shut the gates, and ran to report to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was playing ball in Qingsi Hall. The eunuchs who saw them fled inside, shut the gates, and ran to warn him.

sentences.zh: 盜尋斬關而入。

translations.literal: The robbers soon cut through the gate and entered.
translations.idiomatic: The intruders soon cut through the gate and entered.

sentences.zh: 先是右神策中尉梁守謙有寵於上，每兩軍角伎藝，上常佑右軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Right Divine Strategy Army Director Liang Shouqian had enjoyed the emperor's favor; whenever the two armies competed in skill, the emperor usually aided the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: Right Divine Strategy Army Director Liang Shouqian had long enjoyed the emperor's favor; whenever the two armies competed in contests, the emperor usually backed the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 至是，上狼狽欲幸右軍，左右曰：「右軍遠，恐遇盜，不若幸左軍近。

translations.literal: At this moment the emperor in disarray wished to go to the Right Army; those beside him said: 'The Right Army is far — you may meet robbers; better to go to the nearer Left Army.'
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor in panic wished to flee to the Right Army, but his attendants said, 'The Right Army is far and you may meet the intruders — better the nearer Left Army.'

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 左神策中尉河中馬存亮聞上至，走出迎，捧上足涕泣，自負上入軍中，遣大將康藝全將騎卒入宮討賊。

translations.literal: Left Divine Strategy Army Director Ma Cunliang of Hezhong, hearing the emperor had arrived, ran out to welcome him, embraced the emperor's feet weeping, carried him on his back into the army camp, and dispatched Grand General Kang Yiquan to lead cavalry into the palace to suppress the robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Left Divine Strategy Army Director Ma Cunliang of Hezhong ran out to meet him, embraced his feet weeping, carried him into camp, and sent Grand General Kang Yiquan with cavalry into the palace to suppress the intruders.

sentences.zh: 上憂二太后隔絕，存亮復以五百騎迎二太后至軍。

translations.literal: The emperor worried that the two empress dowagers were cut off; Cunliang again with five hundred cavalry brought both empress dowagers to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the two empress dowagers were cut off, Cunliang sent five hundred cavalry to bring them to the camp.

sentences.zh: 張韶升清思殿，坐御榻，與蘇玄明同食，曰：「果如子言！

translations.literal: Zhang Shao ascended Qingsi Hall, sat on the imperial couch, and ate with Su Xuanming, saying: 'It is indeed as you said!'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao entered Qingsi Hall, sat on the imperial couch, and ate with Su Xuanming, saying, 'It is just as you said!'

sentences.zh: 」玄明驚曰：「事止此邪！

translations.literal: Xuanming said in alarm: 'The affair stops only here!'
translations.idiomatic: Xuanming cried in alarm, 'Is this all there is to it!'

sentences.zh: 」韶懼而走。

translations.literal: Shao in fear fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shao fled in fear.

sentences.zh: 會康藝全與右軍兵馬使尚國忠引兵至，合擊之，殺韶、玄明及其黨，死者狼藉。

translations.literal: Just then Kang Yiquan and Right Army Cavalry Commissioner Shang Guozhong arrived with troops; joining forces they attacked and killed Shao, Xuanming, and their faction; the dead lay strewn about.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yiquan and Right Army Cavalry Commissioner Shang Guozhong arrived with troops, joined battle, and killed Shao, Xuanming, and their followers; corpses lay strewn about.

sentences.zh: 逮夜始定，餘黨猶散匿禁苑中。

translations.literal: Only at night was order restored; remaining faction members still hid scattered in the forbidden park.
translations.idiomatic: Order was restored only at night; survivors still hid in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 明日，悉擒獲之。

translations.literal: The next day they were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they were all captured.

sentences.zh: 時宮門皆閉，上宿於左軍，中外不知上所在，人情恇駭。

translations.literal: At that time all palace gates were closed; the emperor lodged in the Left Army, and inside and outside the court did not know where the emperor was — people's hearts were fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The palace gates were closed and the emperor lodged in the Left Army; court and capital did not know where he was, and panic spread.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，上還宮，宰相帥百官詣延英門賀，來者不過數十人。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, the emperor returned to the palace; the chief ministers led the hundred officials to Yanying Gate to congratulate, but those who came were no more than several tens.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day the emperor returned to the palace. Chief ministers led officials to Yanying Gate to congratulate, but fewer than thirty came.

sentences.zh: 盜所歷諸門，監門宦者三十五人法當死。

translations.literal: At every gate the robbers had passed, thirty-five gate-keeping eunuchs were by law subject to death.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-five gate-keeping eunuchs at the gates the intruders passed were by law subject to death.

sentences.zh: 己亥，詔並杖之，仍不改職任。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, an edict ordered them all flogged but their offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day an edict ordered them flogged but kept in office.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，厚賞兩軍立功將士。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, the two armies' meritorious officers and soldiers were richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day the meritorious soldiers of both armies were richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙卯，以使部侍郎李程、戶部侍郎、判度支竇易直並同平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day yimao, Ministry of Rites Vice Director Li Cheng and Vice Minister of Revenue and Acting Revenue Commissioner Dou Yizhi were both made Associate Chief Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the yimao day, Vice Director Li Cheng and Vice Minister of Revenue Dou Yizhi, acting revenue commissioner, were both made associate chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 上問相於李逢吉，逢吉列上當時大臣有資望者，程為之首，故用之。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Fengji about chief ministers; Fengji listed the great ministers of the time with senior standing, with Cheng at the head, and therefore he was used.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Fengji about chief ministers; Fengji listed senior statesmen with Cheng first, and Cheng was appointed.

sentences.zh: 上好治宮室，欲營別殿，制度甚廣，李程諫，請以所具木石回奉山陵，上即從之。

translations.literal: The emperor loved building palaces and wished to construct a separate hall on a very large scale; Li Cheng remonstrated and asked that the prepared timber and stone be turned instead to supply the imperial tomb; the emperor immediately followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved building palaces and planned a vast new hall. Li Cheng remonstrated and asked that the timber and stone be used for the imperial tomb instead; the emperor at once agreed.

sentences.zh: 六月，己卯朔，以左神策大將軍康藝全為鄜坊節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day jimao, Left Divine Strategy Army Grand General Kang Yiquan was appointed military governor of Bianfang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the jimao new-moon day, Left Divine Strategy Grand General Kang Yiquan was appointed military governor of Bianfang.

sentences.zh: 上聞王庭湊屠牛元翼家，歎宰輔非才，使凶賊縱暴。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Wang Tingcou had slaughtered Niu Yuanji's family and sighed that the chief ministers lacked talent, allowing fierce bandits to run wild.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Wang Tingcou had slaughtered Niu Yuanji's family, the emperor sighed that his chief ministers lacked talent and let fierce rebels run wild.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士韋處厚因上疏言：「裴度勳高中夏，聲播外夷，若置之巖廊，委其參決，河北、山東必稟朝算。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Wei Chuhou thereupon submitted a memorial, saying: 'Pei Du's merit towers in the central summer; his fame spreads among foreign tribes. If he is placed in the hall of state and entrusted with deliberation, Hebei and Shandong will surely follow the court's plans.'
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Wei Chuhou memorialized that Pei Du's merit towered at court and his fame reached foreign lands; if restored to the council and entrusted with deliberation, Hebei and Shandong would surely follow the court's plans.

sentences.zh: 管仲曰：『人離而聽之則愚，合而聽之則聖。

translations.literal: Guan Zhong said: "If one listens to men separately, one is foolish; if one listens to them together, one is sage."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong said, 'Listen to men separately and you are foolish; listen to them together and you are wise.'

sentences.zh: 』理亂之本，非有他術，順人則理，違人則亂。

translations.literal: 'The root of order and disorder has no other art: follow the people and there is order; oppose the people and there is disorder.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The root of order and disorder has no other secret: follow the people and there is order; defy them and there is chaos.'

sentences.zh: 伏承陛下當食歎息，恨無蕭、曹，今有一裴度尚不能留，此馮唐所以謂漢文得廉頗、李牧不能用也。

translations.literal: 'I humbly hear that Your Majesty sighed at mealtime, regretting the lack of a Xiao or Cao; now there is one Pei Du who still cannot be retained — this is why Feng Tang said that Emperor Wen of Han obtained Lian Po and Li Mu but could not use them.'
translations.idiomatic: 'I hear Your Majesty sighed at table, lamenting the lack of men like Xiao He or Cao Shen; yet one Pei Du cannot be kept — this is why Feng Tang said Emperor Wen obtained Lian Po and Li Mu but could not use them.'

sentences.zh: 夫御宰相，當委之，信之，親之，禮之，於事不效，於國無勞，則置之散寮，黜之遠郡。

translations.literal: 'In governing chief ministers, one should entrust them, trust them, draw them close, and honor them; if affairs are ineffective and the state gains no benefit, then place them in idle posts or dismiss them to distant prefectures.'
translations.idiomatic: 'In governing chief ministers, entrust them, trust them, draw them close, and honor them; if they fail in office and serve the state no good, place them in idle posts or send them to distant commands.'

sentences.zh: 如此，則在位者不敢不厲，將進者不敢苟求。

translations.literal: 'Thus those in office will not dare fail to exert themselves, and those about to advance will not dare seek office carelessly.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Then those in office will not dare slacken, and those seeking promotion will not dare scheme.'

sentences.zh: 臣與逢吉素無私嫌，嘗為裴度無辜貶官。

translations.literal: 'Your servant has never had private enmity with Fengji; I once spoke for Pei Du's innocent demotion.'
translations.idiomatic: 'I have no private quarrel with Fengji; I once spoke up when Pei Du was unjustly demoted.'

sentences.zh: 今之所陳，上答聖明，下達群議耳。

translations.literal: 'What I now state answers the sage clarity above and conveys the collective discussion below, that is all.'
translations.idiomatic: 'What I now say answers Your Majesty's wisdom and voices what many discuss.'

sentences.zh: 」上見度奏狀無平章事，以問處厚。

translations.literal: The emperor saw that Du's memorial bore no title of chief minister and asked Chuhou about it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noticed Du's memorial lacked the chief minister title and asked Chuhou about it.

sentences.zh: 處厚具言李逢吉排沮之狀。

translations.literal: Chuhou fully explained how Li Fengji had excluded and obstructed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou fully explained how Li Fengji had blocked him.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何至是邪！

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'How could it come to this!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'How could it come to this!'

sentences.zh: 」李程亦勸上加禮於度。

translations.literal: Li Cheng also urged the emperor to add honors for Du.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng also urged the emperor to honor Du.

sentences.zh: 丙申，加度同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, Du was given the additional title of Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day Du was made Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 張韶之亂，馬存亮功為多，存亮不自矜，委權求出。

translations.literal: In Zhang Shao's disturbance Ma Cunliang's merit was greatest, yet Cunliang did not pride himself on it and, relinquishing power, sought to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhang Shao's disturbance Ma Cunliang's merit was greatest, yet he did not boast and sought to leave office.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以存亮為淮南監軍使。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, Cunliang was made army supervising commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Cunliang was made army supervising commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 夏綏節度使李祐入為左金吾大將軍，壬申，進馬百五十匹，上卻之。

translations.literal: Xiasui Military Governor Li You entered [the capital] as Left Golden Crow Grand General; on the day renshen he presented one hundred and fifty horses; the emperor declined them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiasui Military Governor Li You entered the capital as Left Golden Crow Grand General; on the renshen day he presented one hundred and fifty horses, which the emperor declined.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，侍御史溫造於閣內奏彈祐違敕進奉，請論如法，詔釋之。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, Attending Censor Wen Zao memorialized in the hall impeaching You for presenting tribute in violation of the edict and asked that he be judged according to law; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day Attending Censor Wen Zao impeached You in court for presenting tribute in violation of the edict and asked that he be punished by law; an edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 祐謂人曰：』吾夜半入蔡州城取吳元濟，未嘗心動，今日膽落於溫御史矣！

translations.literal: Li You said to people: 'When I entered Cai Prefecture city at midnight to capture Wu Yuanji, my heart never once faltered; today my gall has fallen to Censor Wen!'
translations.idiomatic: Li You said to others: 'When I stormed Cai Prefecture at midnight and seized Wu Yuanji, my heart never wavered—but today Censor Wen has scared the wits out of me!'

sentences.zh: 八月，丁卯朔，安南奏黃蠻入寇。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day of the month (dingmao), Annan reported that the Yellow Barbarians raided.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the first day (dingmao), Annan reported that the Yellow Barbarians had invaded.

sentences.zh: 龍州刺史尉遲銳上言：「牛心山素稱神異，有掘斷處，請加補塞。

translations.literal: Long Prefecture Inspector Yuchi Rui memorialized: "Ox-Heart Mountain has long been called supernatural; there is a place where it was dug through—please add repair and blocking."
translations.idiomatic: Long Prefecture Inspector Yuchi Rui submitted a memorial: "Ox-Heart Mountain has always been reputed miraculous; a section has been excavated through—please order it repaired and sealed."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 役數萬人於絕險之地，東川為之疲弊。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of men were put to labor in utterly perilous terrain; Eastern Chuan was worn out by it.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of laborers were deployed in treacherous heights, and Eastern Chuan was exhausted by the project.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁未，波斯李蘇沙獻沉香亭子材。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the dingwei day, Li Susa of Persia presented timber for an agarwood pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the dingwei day, Li Susa of Persia presented lumber for a pavilion of agarwood.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺李漢上言：「此何異瑤台、瓊室！

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Official Li Han memorialized: "How is this different from Jasper Terraces and Jade Chambers!"
translations.idiomatic: Left Remonstrance Official Li Han memorialized: "How is this any different from the Jasper Terraces and Jade Chambers!"

sentences.zh: 」上雖怒，亦優容之。

translations.literal: " Although the emperor was angry, he also treated him leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Though angry, the emperor nonetheless treated him with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 漢，道明之六世孫也。

translations.literal: Han was a sixth-generation descendant of Daoming.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han was a sixth-generation descendant of Li Daoming.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊戌，翰林學士韋處厚諫上宴游曰：「先帝以酒色致疾損壽，臣是時不死諫者，以陛下年已十五故也。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the wuxu day, Hanlin Academician Wei Chuhou admonished the emperor about feasting and travel, saying: "The former emperor ruined his health and shortened his life through wine and women; the reason your servant did not remonstrate unto death at that time was that Your Majesty was already fifteen."
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the wuxu day, Hanlin Academician Wei Chuhou admonished the emperor about his revels: "The late emperor impaired his health and shortened his life with wine and women. I did not risk my life remonstrating then because Your Majesty was already fifteen."

sentences.zh: 今皇子才一歲，臣安敢畏死而不諫乎！

translations.literal: Now the crown prince is only one year old—how dare your servant fear death and not remonstrate!
translations.idiomatic: Now the crown prince is only a year old—how can I shrink from death and refuse to speak!

sentences.zh: 」上感其言，賜錦彩百匹、銀器四。

translations.literal: " The emperor was moved by his words and bestowed one hundred bolts of brocade and four silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his words, the emperor bestowed one hundred bolts of brocade and four silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊午，安南奏：黃蠻與環王合兵攻陷陸州，殺刺史葛維。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the wuwu day, Annan reported: the Yellow Barbarians joined with the king of Huan in arms, attacked and captured Luzhou, and killed Prefect Ge Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the wuwu day, Annan reported that the Yellow Barbarians had allied with Huan and stormed Luzhou, killing Prefect Ge Wei.

sentences.zh: 庚申，葬睿聖文惠孝皇帝於光陵，廟號穆宗。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day the Sagely, Cultured, Gracious, and Filial Emperor was buried at Guang Mausoleum; his temple name was Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day Emperor Muzong—posthumously titled the Sagely, Cultured, Gracious, and Filial Emperor—was interred at Guang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 王播以錢十萬緡賂王守澄，求復領利權，十二月，癸未，諫議大夫獨孤朗、張仲方、起居郎柳公權、起居舍人宋申錫、拾遺李景讓、薛廷老請開延英論其奸邪。

translations.literal: Wang Bo used one hundred thousand strings of cash to bribe Wang Shoucheng, seeking to regain control of profit monopolies; in the twelfth month, on the guwei day, Remonstrance Officials Dugu Lang, Zhang Zhongfang, Diarist Liu Gongquan, Diarist-Recorder Song Shenxi, and Remonstrance Officials Li Jingrang and Xue Tinglao asked to open Yanying Hall to discuss his wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo bribed Wang Shoucheng with one hundred thousand strings of cash to regain lucrative offices. In the twelfth month, on the guwei day, Remonstrance Officials Dugu Lang, Zhang Zhongfang, Diarist Liu Gongquan, Diarist-Recorder Song Shenxi, and Remonstrance Officials Li Jingrang and Xue Tinglao petitioned to debate his corruption in Yanying Hall.

sentences.zh: 上問：「前廷爭者不在中邪？

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "Were not those who argued in court earlier among the central officials?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Weren't the men who spoke up in court earlier already in central office?"

sentences.zh: 」即日，除劉栖楚諫議大夫。

translations.literal: " That same day Liu Qichu was appointed Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Liu Qichu was made Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 景讓，憕之曾孫；

translations.literal: Jingrang was the great-grandson of Li Ping;
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingrang was the great-grandson of Li Ping;

sentences.zh: 廷老，河中人也。

translations.literal: Tinglao was a man of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Tinglao was from Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚寅，加天平節度使烏重胤同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the gengyin day, Tianping Military Governor Wu Chongyin was promoted to Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the gengyin day, Tianping Military Governor Wu Chongyin was made Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 乙未，徐泗觀察使王智興以上生日，請於泗州置戒壇，度僧尼以資福，許之。

translations.literal: On the yimao day Xu-Si Military Commissioner Wang Zhixing, because it was the emperor's birthday, asked to establish an ordination platform at Sizhou to tonsure monks and nuns for merit; it was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day Wang Zhixing, commissioner of Xu-Si, petitioned—since it was the emperor's birthday—to set up an ordination platform at Sizhou to tonsure monks and nuns for blessing; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 自元和以來，敕禁此弊，智興欲聚貨，首請置之，於是四方輻湊，江、淮尤甚，智興家貲由此累巨萬。

translations.literal: Since the Yuanhe era edicts had forbidden this abuse, Zhixing wished to gather wealth and was first to request it; thereupon the four quarters converged, especially the Jiang and Huai regions, and Zhixing's household wealth thereby accumulated to tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edicts since the Yuanhe era had forbidden this abuse, but Zhixing sought profit and was the first to ask; soon donors streamed in from every direction, especially along the Jiang and Huai, and his family wealth swelled to tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使李德裕上言：「若不鈐制，至降誕日方停，計兩浙、福建當失六十萬丁。

translations.literal: Zhexi Military Commissioner Li Deyu memorialized: "If it is not restrained, it will not stop until the emperor's birthday; it is estimated that the two Zhes and Fujian will lose six hundred thousand adult males."
translations.idiomatic: Zhexi Military Commissioner Li Deyu memorialized: "Unless this is checked, it will run until the emperor's birthday; the two Zhe circuits and Fujian stand to lose six hundred thousand men of tax age."

sentences.zh: 」奏至，即日罷之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial arrived, it was abolished the same day.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the memorial arrived, the practice was halted that day.

sentences.zh: 是歲，回鶻崇德可汗卒，弟曷薩特勒立。

translations.literal: That year the Uighur Chongde Khaghan died; his younger brother Yisadulu Teqin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Uighur Chongde Khaghan died, and his younger brother Yisadulu Teqin took the throne.

sentences.zh: 敬宗睿武昭愍孝皇帝

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong, Sagely Martial, Illustrious, Lamented, and Filial
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong, the Sagely Martial, Illustrious, Lamented, and Filial Emperor

sentences.zh: 敬宗睿武昭愍孝皇帝寶歷元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong, Sagely Martial, Illustrious, Lamented, and Filial—first year of Baoli (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong, the Sagely Martial, Illustrious, Lamented, and Filial Emperor—first year of Baoli (

sentences.zh: 乙巳，公元八二五年）

translations.literal: yisi, AD 825)
translations.idiomatic: yisi, AD 825)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛亥，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the xinhai day, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the xinhai day, the emperor offered sacrifice at the Southern Suburbs.

sentences.zh: 還，御丹鳳樓，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On returning he held court at Danfeng Tower, amnestied the empire, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he took the throne at Danfeng Tower, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 先是鄠令崔發聞外喧囂，問之，曰：「五坊人毆百姓。

translations.literal: Earlier, E County Magistrate Cui Fa heard an uproar outside and asked about it; he was told, "Men of the Five Wards are beating commoners."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Fa, magistrate of E County, heard a commotion outside and inquired; he was told, "Men of the Five Wards are beating commoners."

sentences.zh: 」發怒，命擒以入，曳之於庭。

translations.literal: " Fa grew angry and ordered them seized and dragged into the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Fa ordered the men seized and hauled into the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 時已昏黑，良久，詰之，乃中使也。

translations.literal: By then it was already dark; after lengthy questioning, they turned out to be palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Night had fallen; only after prolonged questioning did he learn they were palace emissaries.

sentences.zh: 上怒，收發，系御史台。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, arrested Fa, and imprisoned him in the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, had Fa arrested, and confined him in the Censorate prison.

sentences.zh: 是日，發與諸囚立金雞下，忽有品官數十人執梃亂捶發，破面折齒，絕氣乃去。

translations.literal: That day Fa stood with the other prisoners beneath the golden rooster; suddenly several dozen ranking officials wielding clubs beat Fa at random, breaking his face and teeth; they left only when he stopped breathing.
translations.idiomatic: That day, as Fa stood with the other prisoners beneath the golden rooster, dozens of ranking officials suddenly rushed in with clubs and beat him savagely, smashing his face and breaking his teeth; they withdrew only when he ceased to breathe.

sentences.zh: 數刻而蘇，復有繼來求擊之者，台吏以席蔽之，僅免。

translations.literal: After several moments he revived; more came seeking to strike him, but Censorate clerks shielded him with mats and he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later he revived; when more assailants arrived, the jail clerks covered him with mats and he barely survived.

sentences.zh: 上命復系發於台獄而釋諸囚。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Fa re-imprisoned in the Censorate jail and released the other prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Fa returned to the Censorate prison and released the other inmates.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同平章事牛僧孺以上荒淫，嬖倖用事，又畏罪不敢言，但累表求出。
