translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister Niu Sengru, because the emperor was dissolute, favorites held power, and he also feared punishment and dared not speak, only repeatedly submitted memorials asking to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister Niu Sengru saw the emperor's debauchery and the sway of favorites; fearing reprisal, he dared not speak out and only filed repeated requests to leave court.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，升鄂岳為武昌軍，以僧孺同平章事、充武昌節度使。

translations.literal: On the yimao day E-Yue was promoted to the Wuchang Army; Sengru was made Associate Chief Minister and Military Governor of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day E-Yue was elevated to the Wuchang Army command; Niu Sengru was appointed Associate Chief Minister and Wuchang military governor.

sentences.zh: 中旨復以王播兼鹽鐵轉運使，諫官屢爭之，上皆不納。

translations.literal: By imperial intent Wang Bo was again made concurrent Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner; remonstrance officials repeatedly contested it, but the emperor would accept none of it.
translations.idiomatic: By secret imperial order Wang Bo was again named concurrent Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner; remonstrance officials protested repeatedly, but the emperor refused every appeal.

sentences.zh: 牛僧孺過襄陽，山南東道節度使柳公綽服橐鞬候於館舍，將佐諫曰：「襄陽地高於夏口，此禮太過！

translations.literal: When Niu Sengru passed through Xiangyang, Shannan East Circuit Military Governor Liu Gongchuo, wearing bow-case and quiver, waited upon him at the guest house; his staff remonstrated, saying, "Xiangyang stands higher than Xiakou—this courtesy is excessive!"
translations.idiomatic: As Niu Sengru traveled through Xiangyang, Liu Gongchuo, military governor of Shannan East, met him at the lodge wearing bow-case and quiver on his belt. His officers objected: "Xiangyang ranks above Xiakou—this courtesy goes too far!"

sentences.zh: 」公綽曰：「奇章公甫離台席，方鎮重宰相，所以尊朝廷也。

translations.literal: " Gongchuo said: "Lord Qizhang has just left the central council; a frontier post should honor a chief minister—this is to honor the court."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongchuo replied, "Lord Qizhang has only just left the central council; a frontier command should honor a chief minister—this is how we show respect for the throne."

sentences.zh: 」竟行之。

translations.literal: " He carried it out in the end.
translations.idiomatic: He went through with it anyway.

sentences.zh: 上游幸無常，暱比群小，視朝月不再三，大臣罕得進見。

translations.literal: The emperor's outings were irregular; he grew close to petty men; he held court fewer than three times a month; chief ministers rarely gained audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor toured at whim, kept company with low favorites, held court fewer than three times a month, and seldom received his senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬午，浙西觀察使李德裕獻《丹扆六箴》：一曰《宵衣》，以諷視朝稀晚；

translations.literal: In the second month, on the renwu day, Zhexi Military Commissioner Li Deyu presented the "Six Admonitions of the Cinnabar Screen": first, "Night Robes," to admonish rare and late attendance at court;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the renwu day, Zhexi Military Commissioner Li Deyu submitted the Six Admonitions of the Cinnabar Screen: first, "Night Robes," rebuking infrequent and tardy audiences;

sentences.zh: 二曰《正服》，以諷服御乖異；

translations.literal: second, "Correct Attire," to admonish irregular dress and equipage;
translations.idiomatic: second, "Correct Attire," rebuking improper dress and regalia;

sentences.zh: 三曰《罷獻》，以諷徵求玩好；

translations.literal: third, "Cease Presentations," to admonish levying curios and delights;
translations.idiomatic: third, "Cease Presentations," rebuking demands for luxuries and curios;

sentences.zh: 四曰《納誨》，以諷侮棄讜言；

translations.literal: fourth, "Accept Remonstrance," to admonish scorning and discarding forthright counsel;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, "Accept Remonstrance," rebuking contempt for honest advice;

sentences.zh: 五曰《辨邪》，以諷信任群小；

translations.literal: fifth, "Discern Evil," to admonish trusting petty men;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, "Discern Evil," rebuking trust placed in base companions;

sentences.zh: 六曰《防微》，以諷輕出遊幸。

translations.literal: sixth, "Guard the Slight," to admonish lightly going out on pleasure tours.
translations.idiomatic: sixth, "Guard the Slight," rebuking reckless excursions and pleasure travel.

sentences.zh: 其《納誨箴》略曰：「漢驁流湎，舉白浮鐘；

translations.literal: The "Accept Remonstrance" admonition in brief says: "Han dissipation flowed deep in drink, raising white and floating bells;
translations.idiomatic: The Accept Remonstrance admonition reads in part: "The Han emperor drowned in wine, hoisting cups till the bells floated;

sentences.zh: 魏睿侈汰，陵霄作宮。

translations.literal: Wei Ming was extravagant and wasteful, building Lingxiao Palace."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui of Wei was prodigal, raising the Lingxiao Palace."

sentences.zh: 忠雖不忤，善亦不從。

translations.literal: Loyalty though not opposed, good counsel also not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal words met no outright rebuff, yet good counsel went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 以規為瑱，是謂塞聰。

translations.literal: Taking admonition as an ear-plug—this is called blocking the ears.
translations.idiomatic: To treat remonstrance as an ear-plug is to deafen oneself.

sentences.zh: 」《防微箴》曰：「亂臣猖獗，非不遽數。

translations.literal: " The "Guard the Slight" admonition says: "Rebellious ministers run rampant—not that they were not quickly counted."
translations.idiomatic: The Guard the Slight admonition says: "Traitors grow bold—not because their numbers were never reckoned."

sentences.zh: 玄服莫辨，觸瑟始僕。

translations.literal: Black robes could not be distinguished; only when the zither was touched did servants subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: Assassins in dark robes went unrecognized; only when a lute string was brushed did attendants strike them down.

sentences.zh: 柏谷微行，豺豕塞路。

translations.literal: A secret journey to Baigu—wolves and boars blocked the road.
translations.idiomatic: A secret outing to Baigu left wolves and swine crowding the path.

sentences.zh: 睹貌獻餐，斯可戒懼！

translations.literal: To see a face and offer a meal—this can warn and inspire fear!
translations.idiomatic: To read a man's face and set a meal before him—there is a lesson in dread!

sentences.zh: 」上優詔答之。

translations.literal: The emperor replied with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a gracious edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 上既復系崔發於獄，給事中李渤上言：「縣令不應曳中人，中人不應毆御囚，其罪一也。

translations.literal: After the emperor had again imprisoned Cui Fa, Supervising Secretary Li Bo memorialized: "A county magistrate should not drag a palace attendant; a palace attendant should not beat an imperial prisoner—their offenses are one in kind."
translations.idiomatic: Once Cui Fa was jailed again, Supervising Secretary Li Bo argued: "A magistrate must not haul a palace emissary about, and an emissary must not beat a prisoner of the throne—the fault is equal on both sides."

sentences.zh: 然縣令所犯在赦前，中人所犯在赦後。

translations.literal: Yet the magistrate's offense fell before the amnesty, while the attendants' offenses fell after the amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the magistrate's crime predated the amnesty, while the attendants' crimes came after it.

sentences.zh: 中人橫暴，一至於此。

translations.literal: The attendants' arrogance reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: The emissaries' violence had reached such a pitch.

sentences.zh: 若不早正刑書，臣恐四夷籓鎮聞之，則慢易之心生矣。

translations.literal: If legal punishment is not corrected early, your servant fears that when the four barbarians and frontier commands hear of it, a spirit of contempt will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the law is enforced at once, I fear that when foreign peoples and frontier commands hear of this, they will learn to hold the court in contempt.

sentences.zh: 」諫議大夫張仲方上言，略曰：「鴻恩將佈於天下而不行御前，霈澤遍被於昆蟲而獨遺崔發。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Zhang Zhongfang memorialized, in brief: "Great grace is about to be spread through the empire yet does not reach before the throne; broad favor covers even insects yet Cui Fa alone is left out."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Zhang Zhongfang wrote, in part: "Mercy is to blanket the realm yet cannot reach the emperor's own doorstep; favor is to fall on the smallest creatures yet Cui Fa alone is excluded."

sentences.zh: 」自餘諫官論奏甚眾，上皆不聽。

translations.literal: The remaining remonstrance officials submitted many memorials; the emperor would listen to none.
translations.idiomatic: Other remonstrance officials piled on memorials, but the emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 戊子，李逢吉等從容言於上曰：「崔發輒曳中人，誠大不敬，然其母，故相韋貫之之姊也，年垂八十，自發下獄，積憂成疾。

translations.literal: On the wuzi day Li Fengji and others spoke gently to the emperor, saying: "Cui Fa presumptuously dragged a palace attendant—truly a grave disrespect; yet his mother is the sister of the former chief minister Wei Guanzhi, nearly eighty years old; since Fa entered prison she has piled grief into illness."
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day Li Fengji and others spoke softly to the emperor: "Cui Fa was wrong to seize a palace emissary—indeed a grave breach—but his mother is the sister of former Chief Minister Wei Guanzhi, nearly eighty; since Fa was imprisoned her grief has turned to illness."

sentences.zh: 陛下方以孝理天下，此所宜矜念。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty now governs the empire by filial piety—this is what should be pitied and remembered."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty rules the world through filial piety—surely this merits compassion."

sentences.zh: 」上乃愍然曰：「此諫官但言發冤，未嘗言其不敬，亦不言有老母。

translations.literal: The emperor then said with pity: "These remonstrance officials only spoke of Fa's injustice; they never said he was disrespectful, nor that he had an aged mother."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed: "The remonstrators spoke only of Fa's wrongs; none said he had been disrespectful, and none mentioned his old mother."

sentences.zh: 如卿所言，朕何為不赦之！

translations.literal: "As you speak, why would I not pardon him!"
translations.idiomatic: "If that is so, how could I refuse to pardon him!"

sentences.zh: 」即命中使釋其罪，送歸家，仍慰勞其母。

translations.literal: " He immediately ordered a palace attendant to release his crime and send him home, and also comforted his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He at once ordered a palace attendant to release Fa and send him home, and sent condolences to his mother.

sentences.zh: 母對中使杖發四十。

translations.literal: The mother had the attendant beat Fa forty blows.
translations.idiomatic: The mother then had the attendant flog Fa forty strokes.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛酉，遣司門郎中於人文冊回鶻曷薩特勒為愛登裡囉汩沒密於合毘伽昭禮可汗。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the xinyou day, Director of the Gate Office Yu Renwen was dispatched to enfeoff the Uighur Yisadulu Teqin as Aidengli Luogu Mimi he Hepijia Zhaoli Khaghan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the xinyou day, Yu Renwen of the Gate Office was sent to invest the Uighur Yisadulu Teqin as Aidengli Luogu Mimi he Hepijia Zhaoli Khaghan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸巳，群臣上尊號曰文武大聖廣孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the guisi day, the officials offered the honorific title Civil and Martial Great Sagely Broadly Filial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the guisi day, the court offered the honorific Civil and Martial Great Sagely Broadly Filial Emperor.

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: The empire was amnestied.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 赦文但云：「左降官已經量移者，宜與量移，」不言未量移者。

translations.literal: The amnesty text only said: "Demoted officials who have already been transferred in measure should again be transferred in measure," and did not speak of those not yet transferred.
translations.idiomatic: The amnesty decree said only that demoted officials already given a partial recall "should again be recalled in measure," and said nothing of those not yet recalled at all.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士韋處厚上言：「逢吉恐李紳量移，故有此處置。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Wei Chuhou memorialized: "Fengji feared Li Shen would be transferred, and therefore arranged this wording."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Wei Chuhou wrote: "Fengji feared Li Shen would be recalled, and so engineered this wording."

sentences.zh: 如此，則應近年流貶官，因李紳一人皆不得量移也。

translations.literal: "If so, then all officials banished in recent years, because of Li Shen alone, would none receive transfer."
translations.idiomatic: "At this rate every recent exile would be denied recall—for the sake of one man, Li Shen."

sentences.zh: 」上即追赦文改之。

translations.literal: " The emperor immediately recalled the amnesty text and revised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once recalled the amnesty text and had it rewritten.

sentences.zh: 紳由是得移江州長史。

translations.literal: Shen thereby obtained transfer to Senior Recorder of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen was thereby moved to senior recorder of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲辰，鹽鐵使王播進羨餘絹百萬匹。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the jiachen day, Salt Commissioner Wang Bo presented surplus silk of one million bolts.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the jiachen day, Salt Commissioner Wang Bo presented one million bolts of surplus silk.

sentences.zh: 播領鹽鐵，誅求嚴急，正入不充而羨餘相繼。

translations.literal: Bo headed salt and iron; exactions were severe and urgent; regular revenue did not suffice yet surpluses came in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo ran salt and iron with ruthless levies; ordinary receipts fell short even as "surplus" tribute poured in.

sentences.zh: 己未，詔王播造競渡船二十艘，運材於京師造之，計用轉運半年之費。

translations.literal: On the jiwei day an edict ordered Wang Bo to build twenty dragon-boat racing vessels; materials were transported to the capital for construction, costing half a year's transport expenses.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day the court ordered Wang Bo to build twenty racing boats, shipping timber to the capital for assembly at a cost equal to six months of transport funds.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫張仲方等力諫，乃減其半。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Officials Zhang Zhongfang and others remonstrated forcefully; it was then reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Officials Zhang Zhongfang and others protested vigorously, and the order was cut in half.

sentences.zh: 諫官言京兆尹崔元略以諸父事內常侍崔潭峻。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials said that Jingzhao Magistrate Cui Yuanlue waited upon Palace Attendant Cui Tanjun as upon an uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials charged that Jingzhao Magistrate Cui Yuanlue attended Palace Attendant Cui Tanjun as a nephew would an uncle.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，元略遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: On the dingmao day Yuanlue was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day Cui Yuanlue was moved to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 昭義節度使劉悟方去鄆州也，以鄆兵二千自隨為親兵。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhaoyi Military Governor Liu Wu left Yun Prefecture, he took two thousand Yun troops with him as personal guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaoyi Military Governor Liu Wu had left Yun Prefecture earlier, he kept two thousand Yun soldiers as a personal guard.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚戌，悟暴疾薨，子將作監主簿從諫匿其喪，與大將劉武德及親兵謀，以悟遺表求知留後。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the gengxu day, Wu died suddenly of illness; his son, Chief Secretary of the Directorate of Palace Buildings Congjian, concealed the death and, with Grand General Liu Wude and the personal guard, plotted to use Wu's final memorial to request that Congjian be made acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the gengxu day, Liu Wu died suddenly; his son Congjian, a chief secretary in the palace workshops, hid the corpse and, with General Liu Wude and the guard, planned to use Wu's deathbed memorial to secure Congjian's succession.

sentences.zh: 司馬賈直言入責從諫曰：「爾父提十二州地歸朝廷，其功非細，只以張汶之故，自謂不潔淋頭，竟至羞死。

translations.literal: Assistant Military Governor Jia Zhiyan entered and rebuked Congjian, saying: "Your father brought the lands of twelve prefectures back to the court—his merit was not slight; only because of Zhang Wen did he deem himself defiled from head to foot and in the end died of shame."
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Military Governor Jia Zhiyan burst in and upbraided Congjian: "Your father surrendered twelve prefectures to the throne—no small deed; yet over Zhang Wen he felt himself stained through and shamed unto death."

sentences.zh: 爾孺子，何敢如此！

translations.literal: You rash youth—how dare you act like this!
translations.idiomatic: You reckless boy—how dare you behave thus!

sentences.zh: 父死不哭，何以為人！

translations.literal: Father dead yet no mourning—how can you be called human!
translations.idiomatic: Your father is dead and you will not mourn—what kind of man are you!

sentences.zh: 」從諫恐悚不能對，乃發喪。

translations.literal: " Congjian, fearful and unable to reply, then announced the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian, terrified and speechless, at last proclaimed the funeral.

sentences.zh: 初，陳留人武昭罷石州刺史，為袁王府長史，鬱鬱怨執政。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wu Zhao of Chenliu had been dismissed as prefect of Shi Prefecture and was chief secretary of the Prince of Yuan's household; he brooded in resentment against those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wu Zhao of Chenliu, removed as prefect of Shi, served as chief secretary to the Prince of Yuan and nursed a grudge against the ministers in power.

sentences.zh: 李逢吉與李程不相悅，水部郎中李仍叔，程之族人，激怒之雲，程欲與昭官，為逢吉所沮。

translations.literal: Li Fengji and Li Cheng were at odds; Water Section Director Li Yingshu, a clansman of Cheng, inflamed Zhao with the claim that Cheng wished to give Zhao an office, which Fengji blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji and Li Cheng were estranged; Li Yingshu of the Water Section, a kinsman of Cheng, goaded Zhao with word that Cheng meant to give him a post—only for Fengji to thwart it.

sentences.zh: 昭因酒酣，對左金吾兵曹茅匯言欲刺逢吉，為人所告。

translations.literal: Zhao, deep in wine, told Mao Hui of the Left Golden Crow Army Bureau that he wished to assassinate Fengji, and someone reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, Zhao told Mao Hui of the Left Golden Crow Army Bureau that he meant to stab Fengji; an informer brought word.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚辰，詔三司鞫之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the gengchen day, an edict ordered the Three Offices to try the case.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the gengchen day, the Three Offices were ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 前河陽掌書記李仲言謂匯曰：』君言李程與昭謀則生，不然必死。

translations.literal: Former Heyang Records Officer Li Zhongyan said to Hui: 'If you say Li Cheng plotted with Zhao you will live; otherwise you will surely die.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongyan, formerly records officer at Heyang, told Hui: 'Say that Li Cheng conspired with Zhao and you live; say otherwise and you die.'

sentences.zh: 」匯曰：「冤死甘心！

translations.literal: Hui said: "To die wrongfully—I am willing in heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied, "To die unjustly—I accept it gladly!"

sentences.zh: 誣人自全，匯不為也！

translations.literal: To frame another to save oneself—Hui will not do it!
translations.idiomatic: To frame an innocent man to save my skin—Mao Hui will not do it!

sentences.zh: 」獄成。

translations.literal: " The case was concluded.
translations.idiomatic: The investigation was concluded.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲子，武昭杖死，李仍叔貶道州司馬，李仲言流象州，茅匯流崖州。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day jiazi, Wu Zhao was beaten to death; Li Yingshu was demoted to militia commissioner of Daozhou; Li Zhongyan was exiled to Xiangzhou; and Mao Hui was exiled to Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the tenth month's jiazi day, Wu Zhao was beaten to death. Li Yingshu was demoted to militia commissioner of Daozhou, Li Zhongyan was banished to Xiangzhou, and Mao Hui to Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 上欲幸驪山溫湯，左僕射李絳、諫議大夫張仲方等屢諫不聽，拾遺張權輿伏紫宸殿下，叩頭諫曰：「昔周幽王幸驪山，為犬戎所殺；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to visit the hot springs at Mount Li. The Left Vice Director Li Jiang, Remonstrance and Advice Officer Zhang Zhongfang, and others repeatedly remonstrated but he would not listen. The Reminder Zhang Quanyu lay prostrate below Zichen Hall, knocking his head as he remonstrated, saying: "Of old King You of Zhou visited Mount Li and was killed by the Quanrong;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to visit the hot springs at Mount Li. The Left Vice Director Li Jiang, Remonstrance Officer Zhang Zhongfang, and others remonstrated again and again, but he would not heed them. The Reminder Zhang Quanyu prostrated himself below Zichen Hall and, knocking his head on the ground, remonstrated: "Long ago King You of Zhou visited Mount Li and was killed by the Quanrong;

sentences.zh: 秦始皇葬驪山，國亡；

translations.literal: the First Emperor of Qin was buried at Mount Li and the state perished;
translations.idiomatic: the First Emperor of Qin was buried at Mount Li and his dynasty fell;

sentences.zh: 玄宗宮驪山而祿山亂；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had his palace at Mount Li and An Lushan rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong built his palace at Mount Li and An Lushan rose in rebellion;

sentences.zh: 先帝幸驪山，而享年不長。

translations.literal: the late emperor visited Mount Li and did not enjoy a long span of years.
translations.idiomatic: and the late emperor visited Mount Li and did not live to old age.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「驪山若此之凶邪？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Is Mount Li so very inauspicious?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Is Mount Li truly so ill-omened?

sentences.zh: 我宜一往以驗彼言。

translations.literal: I ought to go once to test their words.
translations.idiomatic: I should go once and put their words to the test."

sentences.zh: 」十一月，庚寅，幸溫湯，即日還宮，謂左右曰：「彼叩頭者之言，安足信哉！

translations.literal: " In the eleventh month, on the day gengyin, he visited the hot springs, returned to the palace the same day, and said to those beside him: "The words of that man who knocked his head—how are they worth believing!
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the gengyin day, he visited the hot springs and returned to the palace the same day. He told his attendants, "What that man who knocked his head said—how is it worth believing!

sentences.zh: 丙申，立皇子普為晉王。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, the emperor established the prince Pu as Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day, Prince Pu was created Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 朝廷得劉悟遺表，議者多言上黨內鎮，與河朔異，不可許。

translations.literal: The court received Liu Wu's final memorial. Many in the debate said that Shangdang is an interior commandery, different from the Hebei north, and could not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the court received Liu Wu's final memorial, many argued that Shangdang was an interior commandery, unlike the Hebei frontier, and that the request could not be granted.

sentences.zh: 左僕射李絳上疏，以為：「兵機尚速，威斷貴定，人情未一，乃可伐謀。

translations.literal: The Left Vice Director Li Jiang submitted a memorial, holding: "Military opportunity favors speed; authority and decision value firmness; when men's hearts are not yet one, then one may attack their schemes.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Vice Director Li Jiang submitted a memorial arguing: "Military opportunity demands speed, and decisive authority must be settled quickly. When hearts are divided, that is when you can overturn their plots.

sentences.zh: 劉悟死已數月，朝廷尚未處分，中外人意，共惜事機。

translations.literal: Liu Wu has been dead for several months, yet the court has still not acted; inside and outside, all alike regret the lost opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu has been dead for months, yet the court still has not decided the matter. At court and in the provinces alike, everyone laments the missed chance.

sentences.zh: 今昭義兵眾，必不盡與從諫同謀，縱使其半葉同，尚有其半效順。

translations.literal: Now the Zhaoyi army masses will certainly not all plot with Congjian; even if half side with him, still half will submit in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhaoyi troops surely do not all stand with Congjian. Even if half join him, the other half will still submit to the throne.

sentences.zh: 從諫未嘗久典兵馬，威惠未加於人。

translations.literal: Congjian has never long commanded troops; authority and grace have not yet been imposed on the men.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian has never held military command for long, and neither authority nor kindness has yet won over the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 又此道素貧，非時必無優賞。

translations.literal: Moreover this circuit has always been poor; except at the right moment there will certainly be no generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit has always been poor, and in ordinary times there are no lavish rewards to offer.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷但速除近澤潞一將充昭義節度使，令兼程赴鎮，從諫未及佈置，新使已至潞州，所謂『先人奪人之心』也。

translations.literal: Now the court need only quickly appoint a general near Ze-Lu as Zhaoyi military commissioner, order him to travel night and day to his post; before Congjian can arrange matters, the new envoy will already be at Luzhou—what is called 'one who arrives first seizes men's hearts.'
translations.idiomatic: The court should promptly appoint a general from the Ze-Lu region as Zhaoyi military commissioner and order him to rush to the post by forced marches. Before Congjian can organize anything, the new commissioner will already be at Luzhou—the classic case of seizing the initiative.

sentences.zh: 新使既至，軍心自有所繫。

translations.literal: Once the new envoy arrives, the army's hearts will naturally have something to attach to.
translations.idiomatic: Once the new commissioner arrives, the troops will naturally have someone else to follow.

sentences.zh: 從諫無位，何名主張，設使謀撓朝命，其將士必不肯從。

translations.literal: Congjian, without position—by what name would he assert himself? Even if he schemes to thwart the court's order, his officers and men will certainly not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Without an appointment, what standing would Congjian have to press his claims? Even if he tried to block the court's decision, his officers and men would not follow him.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷久無處分，彼軍不曉朝廷之意，欲效順則恐忽授從諫，欲同軍惡則恐別更除人，猶豫之間，若有奸人為之畫策，虛張賞設錢數，軍士覬望，尤難指揮。

translations.literal: Now the court has long been without a disposition; that army does not understand the court's intent. Those wishing to submit fear that Congjian may suddenly be appointed; those wishing to join the army's wickedness fear that another man may be appointed instead. In their hesitation, if a villain plots for them and falsely inflates the sums for rewards and distributions, the soldiers will covet them and will be especially hard to command.
translations.idiomatic: The court's long delay has left the army unsure of its intent. Men who want to submit fear Congjian will suddenly be confirmed; men who want to join in rebellion fear someone else will be appointed instead. In that uncertainty, schemers can inflate promised rewards, the soldiers' greed will be stirred, and command will become all the harder.

sentences.zh: 伏望速賜裁斷，仍先下明敕，宣示軍眾，獎其從來忠節，賜新使繒五十萬匹，使之賞設。

translations.literal: I humbly hope for a speedy decision, and also that a clear edict be issued first to show the army masses, praising their constant loyalty, and that five hundred thousand bolts of silk be granted the new envoy for distribution and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to decide at once: issue a clear edict praising the troops' long loyalty, and grant the new commissioner five hundred thousand bolts of silk for rewards and distributions.

sentences.zh: 續除劉從諫一剌史。

translations.literal: Then appoint Liu Congjian to a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Then appoint Liu Congjian to a prefectural post.

sentences.zh: 從諫既粗有所得，必且擇利而行，萬無違拒。

translations.literal: Congjian, having roughly gained something, will certainly choose what profits him and act; there is no chance he will defy.
translations.idiomatic: Once Congjian has gained something tangible, he is sure to take what benefits him and comply—he will not resist.

sentences.zh: 設不從命，臣亦以為不假攻討，何則？

translations.literal: If he does not obey the order, I also think there is no need to borrow an attack—why?
translations.idiomatic: If he still refuses, I believe there is no need for military action either. Why?

sentences.zh: 臣聞從諫已禁山東三州軍士不許自畜兵刀，足明群心殊未得一，帳下之事亦在不疑。

translations.literal: I hear that Congjian has already forbidden soldiers of the three Shandong prefectures from keeping arms and blades privately—enough to show that group hearts are especially not united; matters under his tent are also beyond doubt.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Congjian has already forbidden soldiers in the three eastern prefectures from keeping weapons privately—proof enough that the ranks are far from united and that his own hold on them is shaky.

sentences.zh: 熟計利害，決無即授從諫之理。

translations.literal: On mature consideration of benefit and harm, there is certainly no principle of immediately appointing Congjian.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh the gains and losses carefully, and there is simply no case for confirming Congjian at once.

sentences.zh: 」時李逢吉、王守澄計議已定，竟不用絳等謀。

translations.literal: " At that time Li Fengji and Wang Shoucheng's plans were already settled; in the end they did not use Jiang's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: By then Li Fengji and Wang Shoucheng had already made up their minds, and Li Jiang's plan was never adopted.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛丑，以從諫為昭義留後。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day xinchou, Congjian was made acting regent of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the xinchou day, Congjian was appointed acting military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 劉悟煩苛，從諫濟以寬厚，眾頗附之。

translations.literal: Liu Wu had been vexatious and exacting; Congjian supplemented this with lenience and generosity, and the masses quite attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu had been harsh and finicky; Congjian tempered that with lenience and generosity, and the troops came to favor him.

sentences.zh: 李絳好直言，李逢吉惡之。

translations.literal: Li Jiang loved to speak straight; Li Fengji hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang was fond of blunt counsel; Li Fengji detested him.

sentences.zh: 故事，僕射上日，宰相送之，百官立班，中丞列位於廷，尚書以下每月當牙。

translations.literal: By precedent, on a Vice Director's first audience day the chancellors escorted him, all officials stood in formation, the Censor in Chief took his place in the court, and Vice Ministers and below attended the monthly 'ya' ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, on a Vice Director's first day in office chancellors escorted him, the full bureaucracy stood in formation, the Censor in Chief took his place in the hall, and Vice Ministers and below attended the monthly audience ceremony.

sentences.zh: 元和中，伊慎為僕射，太常博士韋謙上言舊儀太重，削去之。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, when Yin Shen became Vice Director, Academician Wei Qian of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized that the old rites were too heavy and had them cut away.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign, when Yin Shen became Vice Director, Academician Wei Qian of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices argued that the old ceremony was excessive, and it was abolished.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王播恃逢吉之勢，與絳相遇於塗，不之避。

translations.literal: The Censor in Chief Wang Bo relied on Fengji's power; meeting Jiang on the road, he did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Censor in Chief Wang Bo, counting on Fengji's backing, met Jiang on the road and did not step aside.

sentences.zh: 絳引故事上言：「僕射，國初為正宰相，禮數至重。

translations.literal: Jiang cited precedent in a memorial: "The Vice Director, at the dynasty's founding, was the chief chancellor; the ritual weight was utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang cited precedent in a memorial: "At the founding of the dynasty the Vice Director was the chief minister, and the ceremonial honor due him was supreme.

sentences.zh: 倘人才忝位，自宜別授賢良。

translations.literal: If talent unworthily holds the post, one should naturally appoint another worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: If the incumbent lacks the talent for the office, another worthy man should be appointed.

sentences.zh: 若朝命守官，豈得有虧法制。

translations.literal: If the court orders one to hold office, how can the regulations be impaired?
translations.idiomatic: But if the court has ordered a man to hold the post, how can the regulations be set aside?

sentences.zh: 乞下百官詳定。

translations.literal: I beg that this be sent down to all officials for detailed determination.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all officials be ordered to deliberate and settle the matter."

sentences.zh: 」議者多從絳議。

translations.literal: " Many debaters followed Jiang's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Most of those who debated sided with Li Jiang.

sentences.zh: 上聽行舊儀。

translations.literal: The emperor approved restoring the old rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved restoring the old ceremony.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以絳有足疾，除太子少師、分司。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, because Jiang had an ailment of the foot, he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince with detached service.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day, citing Jiang's foot ailment, the emperor made him Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince in a sinecure post away from court.

sentences.zh: 言事者多稱裴度賢，不宜棄之籓鎮，上數遣使至興元勞問度，密示以還期。

translations.literal: Many who spoke on policy praised Pei Du as worthy and said he should not be abandoned in a frontier command; the emperor repeatedly sent envoys to Xingyuan to comfort Du and secretly showed him a date for return.
translations.idiomatic: Many memorializers praised Pei Du as worthy and argued that he should not be left in the provinces. The emperor repeatedly sent envoys to Xingyuan to comfort him and quietly signaled when he might return.

sentences.zh: 度因求入朝，逢吉之黨大懼。

translations.literal: Du therefore requested an audience; Fengji's faction was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Du then asked to come to court, and Fengji's faction was terrified.

sentences.zh: 敬宗睿武昭愍孝皇帝寶歷二年（

translations.literal: Annals of Emperor Jingzong, the Sagely, Martial, Illustrious, and Gracious Filial Emperor — the second year of Baoli (
translations.idiomatic: In the annals of Emperor Jingzong, the Sagely, Martial, Illustrious, and Gracious Filial Emperor, the second year of Baoli (

sentences.zh: 丙年，公元八二六年）

translations.literal: the bing year, corresponding to AD 826)
translations.idiomatic: bing year, AD 826)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬辰，裴度自興元入朝，李逢吉之黨百計毀之。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the day renchen, Pei Du entered court from Xingyuan; Fengji's faction used a hundred schemes to slander him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month's renchen day, Pei Du arrived at court from Xingyuan. Fengji's faction tried every trick to destroy his reputation.

sentences.zh: 先是民間謠云：「緋衣小兒坦其腹，天上有口被驅逐。

translations.literal: Earlier a folk rhyme ran: "A crimson-clad child bares his belly; heaven above has a mouth and is driven away.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a street rhyme had circulated: "A child in crimson bares his belly; heaven bears a mouth and is driven off.

sentences.zh: 」又，長安城中有橫亙六岡，如乾象，度宅偶居第五岡。

translations.literal: " Moreover, in Chang'an city six ridges span the land like the Qian trigram; Du's residence happened to lie on the fifth ridge.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang'an also had six ridges running across it like the Qian hexagram, and Pei Du's house happened to stand on the fifth ridge.

sentences.zh: 張權輿上言：「度名應圖讖，宅占岡原，不召而來，其旨可見。

translations.literal: Zhang Quanyu memorialized: "Du's name answers to prophecy charts; his residence occupies a ridge and plain; uninvited he comes—the intent is visible.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyu memorialized: "Du's name fits the prophecies, his house sits on a dragon ridge, and he has come without being summoned—the meaning is obvious.

sentences.zh: 」上雖年少，悉察其誣謗，待度益厚。

translations.literal: " Though the emperor was young, he fully perceived the slander and treated Du ever more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Though still young, the emperor saw through the smears and treated Du with even greater favor.

sentences.zh: 度初至京師，朝士填門，度留客飲。

translations.literal: When Du first reached the capital, courtiers filled his gate; Du kept guests and drank with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Du first reached the capital, officials thronged his gate. He entertained guests with wine.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹劉棲楚附度耳語，侍御史崔鹹舉觴罰度曰：「丞相不應許所由官呫囁耳語。

translations.literal: The Jingzhao Intendant Liu Qichu leaned toward Du and whispered in his ear. The Attending Censor Cui Xian raised his cup and penalized Du, saying: "A chancellor should not permit a subordinate official to mutter and whisper in his ear.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao Intendant Liu Qichu leaned close and whispered in Du's ear. Attending Censor Cui Xian raised his cup and fined Du, saying, "A chief minister must not let a subordinate official mutter in his ear."

sentences.zh: 」度笑而飲之。

translations.literal: " Du smiled and drank.
translations.idiomatic: Du smiled and drained the cup.

sentences.zh: 棲楚不自安，趨出。

translations.literal: Qichu was ill at ease and hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: Qichu, mortified, rushed away.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁未，以度為司空、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day dingwei, Du was made Minister of Works and Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the dingwei day, Du was appointed Minister of Works and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 度在中書，左右忽白失印。

translations.literal: While Du was at the Secretariat, attendants suddenly reported that the seal was lost.
translations.idiomatic: While Du was at the Secretariat, an attendant suddenly announced that the seal was missing.

sentences.zh: 聞者失色，度飲酒自如。

translations.literal: Those who heard it changed color; Du drank as before.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone present went pale; Du went on drinking as if nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 頃之，左右白復於故處得印，度不應。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward attendants reported that it had been recovered in its old place; Du did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an attendant reported that the seal had reappeared where it belonged. Du made no reply.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，度曰：「此必吏人盜之以印書券耳，急之則投諸水火，緩之則復還故處。

translations.literal: Someone asked the reason. Du said: "This must be clerks who stole it to stamp documents. Press them and they will throw it into fire or water; relax and it returns to its old place.
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, Du said, "Some clerk stole it to stamp documents. Press him and he'll destroy it; leave him alone and it comes back."

sentences.zh: 」人服其識量。

translations.literal: " Men admired his discernment and magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: People marveled at his composure and judgment.

sentences.zh: 上自即位以來，欲幸東都，宰相及朝臣諫者甚眾。

translations.literal: Since his enthronement the emperor had wished to visit the Eastern Capital; chancellors and courtiers who remonstrated were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking the throne the emperor had wanted to visit the Eastern Capital, and a great many chancellors and officials had remonstrated against it.

sentences.zh: 上皆不聽，決意必行，已令度支員外郎盧貞按視，修東都宮闕及道中行宮。

translations.literal: He listened to none of them, resolved that he must go, and had already ordered Lu Zhen, an aide in the Revenue Section, to inspect and repair the Eastern Capital palaces and the way-station palaces along the route.
translations.idiomatic: He would not listen, was determined to go, and had already sent Revenue Section aide Lu Zhen to survey repairs to the Eastern Capital palaces and the roadside lodges along the way.

sentences.zh: 裴度從容言於上曰：「國家本設兩都以備巡幸，自多難以來，茲事遂廢。

translations.literal: Pei Du said calmly to the emperor: "The state originally established two capitals to prepare for imperial tours; since the many calamities this matter has ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du said gently to the emperor, "The empire set up two capitals for imperial tours, but since the rebellions that practice has lapsed.

sentences.zh: 今宮闕、營壘、百司廨捨率已荒阤，陛下倘欲行幸，宜命有司歲月間徐加完葺，然後可往。

translations.literal: Now palaces, camps, and the government halls of the hundred offices are mostly in ruins. If Your Majesty wishes to travel, you should order the responsible offices over the course of months to restore them slowly, and only then may you go.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces, barracks, and government offices are mostly in ruins. If Your Majesty still wishes to go, let the responsible offices spend months restoring them gradually, and only then set out."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「從來言事者皆雲不當往，如卿所言，不往亦可。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Those who have ever remonstrated all said one should not go; as you say, not going is also acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Everyone who has remonstrated has said I should not go. As you put it, staying home is fine too."

sentences.zh: 」會朱克融、王庭湊皆請以兵匠助修東都。

translations.literal: " It happened that Zhu Kerong and Wang Tingcou both requested to send troops and artisans to help repair the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Zhu Kerong and Wang Tingcou both offered troops and craftsmen to help repair the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 三月丁亥，敕以修東都煩擾，罷之，召盧貞還。

translations.literal: On the third month's dinghai day, an edict held that repairing the Eastern Capital was troublesome and abolished the project; Lu Zhen was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: On the third month's dinghai day, an edict canceled the Eastern Capital repairs as too burdensome and recalled Lu Zhen.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝廷遣中使賜朱克融時服，克融以為疏惡，執留敕使。

translations.literal: Earlier the court had sent a palace envoy to bestow seasonal garments on Zhu Kerong; Kerong thought them crude and loathsome and detained the edict envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had sent a palace envoy to present Zhu Kerong with seasonal robes. Kerong judged them shoddy and insulting and held the envoy hostage.

sentences.zh: 又奏「當道今歲將士春衣不足，乞度支給三十萬端匹」，又奏「欲將兵馬及丁匠五千助修宮闕」。

translations.literal: He also memorialized, "This year the soldiers' spring clothing on this circuit is insufficient; I beg the Revenue Section to supply three hundred thousand bolts," and also memorialized, "I wish to lead five thousand troops and artisans to help repair the palace."
translations.idiomatic: He also asked the Revenue Section for three hundred thousand bolts of cloth for his troops' spring uniforms, and offered five thousand soldiers and laborers to help repair the palaces.

sentences.zh: 上患之，以問宰相，欲遣重臣宣慰，仍索敕使。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled by this and asked the chancellors; he wished to send a weighty minister to proclaim comfort and still demand the edict envoy back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was alarmed and consulted the chancellors. He wanted to send a senior envoy to soothe Kerong and recover the detained messenger.

sentences.zh: 裴度對曰：「克融無禮已甚，殆將斃矣！

translations.literal: Pei Du replied: "Kerong's rudeness is already extreme; he is nearly done for!
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du answered, "Kerong's insolence has gone as far as it can—he is nearly finished!

sentences.zh: 譬如猛獸，自於山林中咆哮跳踉，久當自困，必不敢輒離巢穴。

translations.literal: He is like a fierce beast roaring and leaping in the mountain forest; in time he will weary himself and certainly will not dare lightly to leave his lair.
translations.idiomatic: He is like a savage beast roaring and thrashing in the hills: given time he will exhaust himself and will not dare leave his den.

sentences.zh: 願陛下勿遣宣慰，亦勿索敕使，旬日之後，徐賜詔書云：『聞中官至彼，稍失去就，俟還，朕自有處分。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty not to send a comfort mission and also not to demand the edict envoy. After ten days or so, slowly bestow an edict saying: 'I have heard that when the palace envoy reached you he somewhat lost his bearings; when he returns I myself will have a disposition.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty not to send a comforting envoy and not to demand the messenger back. After ten days or so, send a leisurely edict: 'I hear the palace envoy lost his composure at your court; when he returns I will deal with it myself.

sentences.zh: 時服，有司製造不謹，朕甚欲知之，已令區處。

translations.literal: As for the seasonal garments, the responsible offices were not careful in manufacture; I greatly wish to know of it and have already ordered arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: As for the robes, the offices were careless in making them and I very much wish to know how that happened—I have already ordered an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 其將士春衣，從來非朝廷征發，皆本道自備。

translations.literal: The soldiers' spring clothing has never been requisitioned by the court; each circuit has always provided its own.
translations.idiomatic: Spring uniforms for troops have never been issued from the capital; each circuit supplies its own.

sentences.zh: 朕不愛數十萬匹物，但素無此例，不可獨與范陽。

translations.literal: I do not begrudge several hundred thousand bolts of goods, but there has never been this precedent; they cannot be given to Fanyang alone.
translations.idiomatic: I do not begrudge a few hundred thousand bolts of cloth, but there is no precedent for such a grant, and Fanyang alone cannot receive it.

sentences.zh: 』所稱助修宮闕，皆是虛語，若欲直挫其奸，宜云『丁匠宜速遣來，已令所在排比供擬。

translations.literal: ' What they call helping repair the palace is all empty talk. If you wish directly to thwart their trickery, you should say, 'The laborers should be sent quickly; I have already ordered the localities to line up supplies and prepare them.
translations.idiomatic: ' His offer to repair the palaces is empty talk. To strike at his scheme directly, say: 'Send the laborers at once—I have already ordered the prefectures along the route to assemble provisions for them.

sentences.zh: 』彼得此詔，必蒼黃失圖。

translations.literal: ' When they receive this edict they will certainly be flustered and lose their plan.
translations.idiomatic: ' Once he receives that edict he will panic and lose his footing.

sentences.zh: 若且示含容，則云『修宮闕事在有司，不假丁匠遠來。

translations.literal: If for the moment you wish to show forbearance, then say, 'Palace repairs are the business of the responsible offices; there is no need for distant laborers to come.
translations.idiomatic: If you prefer a softer line for now, say: 'Palace repairs are handled by the proper offices; there is no need to send laborers from afar.

sentences.zh: 』如是而已，不足勞聖慮也。

translations.literal: ' That is all; it is not enough to trouble imperial concern.
translations.idiomatic: ' That is enough, and it need not trouble Your Majesty further."

sentences.zh: 」上悅，從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor was pleased and followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and did as Pei Du advised.

sentences.zh: 立才人郭氏為貴妃。

translations.literal: The Talented Lady Guo was established as Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: The Talented Lady Guo was elevated to Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 妃，晉王普之母也。

translations.literal: The consort was the mother of Prince of Jin Pu.
translations.idiomatic: She was the mother of Prince Pu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 橫海節度使李全略薨。

translations.literal: The Henghai military commissioner Li Quanlüe died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quanlüe, military commissioner of Henghai, died.

sentences.zh: 其子副大使同捷擅領留後，重賂鄰道，以求承繼。

translations.literal: His son, the deputy commissioner Tongjie, usurped the acting regency and heavily bribed neighboring circuits to seek succession.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tongjie, the deputy commissioner, seized the post as acting regent and lavished bribes on neighboring circuits to win approval for his succession.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊申，以昭義留後劉從諫為節度使。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day wushen, Liu Congjian, acting regent of Zhaoyi, was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the fourth month's wushen day, Liu Congjian was confirmed from acting regent to full military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 五月，幽州軍亂，殺朱克融及其子延齡，軍中立其少子延嗣主軍務。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Youzhou army mutinied, killed Zhu Kerong and his son Yanling, and in the army installed his younger son Yansi to manage military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Youzhou garrison mutinied, killed Zhu Kerong and his son Yanling, and set up Kerong's younger son Yansi to run the command.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲子，上御三殿，令左右軍、教坊、內園為擊球、手搏、雜戲。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jiazi, the emperor presided in the Three Halls and ordered the Left and Right Armies, the Music Bureau, and the inner gardens to perform polo, hand combat, and miscellaneous games.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the jiazi day, the emperor watched from the Three Halls as the Left and Right Armies, the Music Bureau, and the inner parks staged polo, wrestling, and variety acts.

sentences.zh: 戲酣，有斷臂、碎首者，夜漏數刻乃罷。

translations.literal: When the games grew intense, some had arms severed and heads shattered; the night clepsydra ran several watches before they ended.
translations.idiomatic: The contests grew so fierce that men lost arms and had their skulls smashed. The games did not end until several night watches had passed.

sentences.zh: 己卯，上幸興福寺，觀沙門文漵俗講。

translations.literal: On the day jimao the emperor visited Xingfu Temple to watch the monk Wenji's popular lecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day the emperor visited Xingfu Temple to hear the monk Wenji preach in the vernacular.

sentences.zh: 癸未，衡王絢薨。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei the Prince of Heng, Xuan, died.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day Prince Xuan of Heng died.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，宣索左藏見在銀十萬兩、金七千兩，悉貯內藏，以便賜與。

translations.literal: On the day renchen an imperial order sought one hundred thousand taels of silver and seven thousand taels of gold then on hand in the Left Treasury, all to be stored in the inner treasury for convenient bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day the emperor ordered one hundred thousand taels of silver and seven thousand taels of gold from the Left Treasury moved into the inner vault for ready distribution.

sentences.zh: 道士趙歸真說上以神仙，僧惟貞、齊賢、正簡說上以禱祠求福，皆出入宮禁，上信用其言。

translations.literal: The Daoist Zhao Guizhen persuaded the emperor concerning immortals; the monks Weizhen, Qixian, and Zhengjian persuaded him concerning prayer sacrifices to seek blessing—all entered and left the palace prohibitions, and the emperor trusted their words.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Zhao Guizhen preached immortality to the emperor; the monks Weizhen, Qixian, and Zhengjian urged prayer and sacrifice for fortune. All moved freely in and out of the palace, and the emperor believed them.

sentences.zh: 山人杜景先請遍歷江、嶺，求訪異人。

translations.literal: The mountain man Du Jingxian requested to tour the Jiang and Ling regions broadly to seek strange men.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Du Jingxian asked to travel the Yangzi and Lingnan regions in search of wonder-workers.

sentences.zh: 有潤州人週息元，自言壽數百歲，上遣中使迎之。

translations.literal: There was a man of Runzhou, Zhou Xiyuan, who claimed an age of several hundred years; the emperor sent a palace envoy to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: A Runzhou man named Zhou Xiyuan claimed to be several centuries old, and the emperor sent a palace envoy to escort him to court.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙巳，息元至京師，上館之禁中山亭。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day yisi, Xiyuan reached the capital; the emperor lodged him at Zhongshan Pavilion in the forbidden park.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the yisi day, Xiyuan arrived at the capital and was housed in Zhongshan Pavilion within the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 朱延嗣既得幽州，虐用其人。

translations.literal: Zhu Yansi, having obtained Youzhou, cruelly used its people.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhu Yansi held Youzhou, he oppressed the people brutally.

sentences.zh: 都知兵馬使李載義與弟牙內兵馬使載寧共殺延嗣，並屠其家三百餘人。

translations.literal: The command-and-control military commissioner Li Zaiyi and his younger brother, the inner-army military commissioner Zaining, together killed Yansi and slaughtered more than three hundred members of his household.
translations.idiomatic: Command-and-control commissioner Li Zaiyi and his brother Zaining, commissioner of the inner army, killed Yansi together and massacred more than three hundred of his kin.

sentences.zh: 載義權知留後，九月，數延嗣之罪以聞。

translations.literal: Zaiyi provisionally held the acting regency; in the ninth month he several times reported Yansi's crimes to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi took charge as acting regent and, in the ninth month, repeatedly memorialized the court listing Yansi's crimes.

sentences.zh: 載義，承乾之後也。

translations.literal: Zaiyi was a descendant of Chengqian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zaiyi was a descendant of Li Chengqian.

sentences.zh: 庚申，魏博節度使史憲誠妄奏李同捷為軍士所逐，走歸本道，請束身歸朝。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen the Weibo military commissioner Shi Xiancheng falsely reported that Li Tongjie had been driven out by the soldiers, had fled back to his circuit, and begged to bind his body and return to court.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day Shi Xiancheng, military commissioner of Weibo, falsely reported that Li Tongjie had been expelled by his troops, had fled home, and wished to surrender himself to the throne.

sentences.zh: 尋奏同捷復歸滄州。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter [the court] reported that Tongjie had returned to Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the court reported that Li Tongjie had gone back to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以中書侍郎、同平章事李程同平章事、充河東節度使。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly Appointed Councilor Li Cheng was made Jointly Appointed Councilor and commissioned as military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day Li Cheng, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly Appointed Councilor, was confirmed as councilor and sent out as military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己亥，以李載義為盧龍節度使。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day jihai, Li Zaiyi was made military commissioner of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the tenth month’s jihai day, Li Zaiyi was appointed military commissioner of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲申，以門下侍郎、同平章事李逢吉同平章事、充山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day jiashen, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Jointly Appointed Councilor Li Fengji was made Jointly Appointed Councilor and commissioned as military commissioner of the Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the jiashen day, Li Fengji, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Jointly Appointed Councilor, was confirmed as councilor and posted to the Shannan East Circuit as its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上遊戲無度，狎暱群小，善擊球，好手摶，禁軍及諸道爭獻力士，又以錢萬緡付內園令召募力士，晝夜不離側。

translations.literal: The emperor played without limit, was intimate with petty men, was skilled at polo, loved hand wrestling; the Imperial Army and the various circuits competed to present strongmen, and he also gave ten thousand strings of cash to the director of the inner park to recruit strongmen, who day and night never left his side.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor indulged in games without restraint, kept company with low favorites, excelled at polo, and delighted in hand wrestling. The Imperial Army and every circuit vied to present him with brawny champions, and he also handed ten thousand strings of cash to the director of the inner park to recruit more such men, who stayed at his side day and night.

sentences.zh: 又好深夜自捕狐狸。

translations.literal: He also loved going out late at night to catch foxes himself.
translations.idiomatic: He also liked to go out deep into the night and hunt foxes on his own.

sentences.zh: 性復褊急，力士或恃恩不遜，輒配流、籍沒。

translations.literal: His nature was moreover narrow and impatient; if a strongman took favor and was disrespectful, [the emperor] at once banished him and confiscated his property.
translations.idiomatic: He was besides quick-tempered and unforgiving: when a champion took his favor for granted and showed disrespect, the emperor would immediately have him exiled and his property seized.

sentences.zh: 宦官小過，動遭捶撻，皆怨且懼。

translations.literal: For small faults the eunuchs were frequently beaten with rods; all resented and feared [him].
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs who committed minor offenses were often flogged, and they all nursed resentment and dread.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛丑，上夜獵還宮，與宦官劉克明、田務澄、許文端及擊球軍將蘇佐明、王嘉憲、石從寬、閻惟直等二十八人飲酒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day xinchou, the emperor returned to the palace from a night hunt and drank wine with the eunuchs Liu Keming, Tian Wucheng, and Xu Wenduan, and with the polo-army generals Su Zuoming, Wang Jiaxian, Shi Congkuan, Yan Weizhi, and twenty-eight men in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the xinchou day, the emperor came back to the palace from a night hunt and drank with the eunuchs Liu Keming, Tian Wucheng, and Xu Wenduan, together with the polo generals Su Zuoming, Wang Jiaxian, Shi Congkuan, Yan Weizhi, and twenty-five others—twenty-eight men in all.

sentences.zh: 上酒酣，入室更衣，殿上燭忽滅，蘇佐明等弒上於室內。

translations.literal: When the emperor was deep in wine he entered a room to change clothes; the candles in the hall suddenly went out, and Su Zuoming and the others assassinated the emperor in the room.
translations.idiomatic: When he was drunk he went inside to change clothes. The candles in the hall suddenly went dark, and Su Zuoming and his companions murdered the emperor in the chamber.

sentences.zh: 劉克明等矯稱上旨，命翰林學士路隋草遺制，以絳王悟權句當軍國事。

translations.literal: Liu Keming and the others forged the emperor's order, commanding the Hanlin academician Lu Sui to draft a testamentary edict appointing Prince Jiang Wu to provisionally attend to state and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Keming and the rest forged an imperial command ordering Hanlin academician Lu Sui to draft a deathbed edict placing the Crimson Prince, Li Wu, in provisional charge of state and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，宣遺制，絳王見宰相百官於紫宸外廡。

translations.literal: On the day renyin the testamentary edict was proclaimed, and Prince Jiang received the chief ministers and the hundred officials in the outer corridor of Zichen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day the testament was announced, and the Crimson Prince met the chief ministers and the full bureaucracy in the outer corridor of Zichen Hall.

sentences.zh: 克明等欲易置內侍之執權者，於是樞密使王守澄、楊承和、中尉魏從簡、梁守謙定議，以衛兵迎江王涵入宮，發左、右神策、飛龍兵進討賊黨，盡斬之。

translations.literal: Keming and the others wished to replace the inner attendants who held power; thereupon the commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Shoucheng and Yang Chenghe, and the grand marshals Wei Congjian and Liang Shouqian, reached a decision to use palace guards to welcome Prince Jiang Han into the palace, and dispatched the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies and the Flying Dragon Army to advance against the rebel party and behead them all.
translations.idiomatic: Keming's faction meant to displace the powerful eunuchs at court. The commissioners of military affairs Wang Shoucheng and Yang Chenghe, together with the grand marshals Wei Congjian and Liang Shouqian, then resolved to bring the River Prince, Li Han, into the palace with palace guards, and sent the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies and the Flying Dragon Army to attack the rebels and execute every one of them.

sentences.zh: 克明赴井，出而斬之。

translations.literal: Keming threw himself into a well; [they] pulled him out and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Keming threw himself down a well; they hauled him out and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 絳王為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: Prince Jiang was killed by the disorderly troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Crimson Prince perished at the hands of the mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 時事起蒼猝，守澄等以翰林學士韋處厚博通古今，一夕處置，皆與之共議。

translations.literal: At the time the affair had arisen in haste; Shoucheng and the others, because the Hanlin academician Wei Chuhou was broadly versed in past and present, discussed with him overnight every disposition to be made.
translations.idiomatic: Events had erupted too suddenly for orderly procedure. Shoucheng and his allies, knowing that Hanlin academician Wei Chuhou was deeply learned in history, spent the night consulting him on every step they took.

sentences.zh: 守澄等欲號令中外，而疑所以為辭。

translations.literal: Shoucheng and the others wished to issue commands to the court and the realm, but were uncertain what language to use.
translations.idiomatic: They wanted to proclaim their authority throughout the palace and the empire, yet could not settle on the right words.

sentences.zh: 處厚曰：「正名討罪，於義何嫌，安可依違，有所諱避！

translations.literal: Chuhou said: "To rectify names and punish crime—what scruple is there in righteousness? How can one vacillate and shrink from speaking plainly!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chuhou said, "To set the record straight and punish crime is plainly righteous. Why hesitate or trim your language?"

sentences.zh: 」又問：』江王當如何踐祚？

translations.literal: " They again asked: "How should Prince Jiang take the throne?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked again, "How should the River Prince ascend the throne?"

sentences.zh: 」處厚曰：「詰朝，當以王教佈告中外以已平內難。

translations.literal: " Chuhou said: "At dawn tomorrow you should issue a princely edict announcing to the court and the realm that the internal turmoil has been settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chuhou answered, "At dawn tomorrow issue a princely proclamation telling the court and the empire that the palace rebellion has been put down.

sentences.zh: 然後群臣三表勸進，以太皇太后令冊命即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Then let the ministers present three memorials urging enthronement, and by the Grand Empress Dowager's order enfeoff him and have him immediately assume the imperial position."
translations.idiomatic: Then have the ministers submit three memorials urging him to reign, and by order of the Grand Empress Dowager invest him and seat him on the throne."

sentences.zh: 」當時皆從其言，時不暇復問有司，凡百儀法，皆出於處厚，無不葉宜。

translations.literal: " At the time all followed his words; there was no leisure to consult the responsible offices again; of the hundred rites, all issued from Chuhou, and none was inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone followed his advice. There was no time to consult the ritual offices; every ceremony that night was shaped by Wei Chuhou, and none of it misfired.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以裴度攝塚宰。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, Pei Du was appointed acting regent of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day Pei Du was named acting regent of the realm.

sentences.zh: 百官謁見江王於紫宸外廡，王素服涕泣。

translations.literal: The hundred officials paid their respects to Prince Jiang in the outer corridor of Zichen Hall; the prince wore plain robes and wept.
translations.idiomatic: The full bureaucracy paid court to the River Prince in the outer corridor of Zichen Hall. He wore mourning dress and wept.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，見諸軍使於少陽院。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen he received the various army commissioners in Shaoyang Courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day he received the military commissioners of the various armies in Shaoyang Courtyard.

sentences.zh: 趙歸真等諸術士及敬宗時佞幸者，皆流嶺南或邊地。

translations.literal: Zhao Guizhen and the other alchemists, and those who had flattered power in Jingzong's time, were all exiled to Lingnan or the frontier regions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guizhen and the other wonder-workers, together with the sycophants of Jingzong's reign, were all banished to Lingnan or the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 乙已，文宗即位，更名昂。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, Wenzong took the throne and changed his name to Ang.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day Wenzong ascended the throne and took the personal name Ang.

sentences.zh: 戊申，尊母蕭氏為皇太后，王太后為寶歷太后。

translations.literal: On the day wushen his mother the Lady Xiao was honored as Empress Dowager, and Empress Dowager Wang was honored as Baoli Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day his mother, Lady Xiao, was elevated to Empress Dowager, and Empress Dowager Wang was given the title Baoli Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 是時，郭太后居興慶宮，王太后居義安殿，蕭太后居大內。

translations.literal: At this time Grand Empress Dowager Guo resided in Xingqing Palace, Empress Dowager Wang in Yi'an Hall, and Empress Dowager Xiao in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Empress Dowager Guo lived in Xingqing Palace, Empress Dowager Wang in Yi'an Hall, and Empress Dowager Xiao within the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 上性孝謹，事三宮如一，每得珍異之物，先薦郊廟，次奉三宮，然後進御。

translations.literal: The emperor by nature was filial and careful; he served the three palaces as one, and whenever he obtained rare and precious things he first offered them at the suburban altars, next presented them to the three palaces, and only then brought them into the imperial apartments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was by nature reverent and dutiful. He treated the three palaces with equal devotion, and whenever he received a rare treasure he first offered it at the suburban shrines, then sent it to the three palaces, and only afterward kept it for his own use.

sentences.zh: 蕭太后，閩人也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xiao was a native of Min.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xiao came from Min.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以翰林學士韋處厚為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu the Hanlin academician Wei Chuhou was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly Appointed Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day Hanlin academician Wei Chuhou was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly Appointed Councilor.

sentences.zh: 上自為諸王，深知兩朝之弊，及即位，勵精求治，去奢從儉。

translations.literal: Since he had been a prince the emperor had deeply known the abuses of the two preceding reigns; when he took the throne he strove in spirit to seek good government and abandoned extravagance for thrift.
translations.idiomatic: As a prince he had seen clearly how the two previous reigns had gone wrong. Once enthroned he threw himself into reform and turned from luxury to restraint.

sentences.zh: 詔宮女非有職掌者皆出之，出三千餘人。

translations.literal: He ordered that palace women who had no official duties all be released; more than three thousand were sent out.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed that every palace woman without an assigned office be released—more than three thousand left the palace.

sentences.zh: 五坊鷹犬，准元和故事，量留校獵外，悉放之。

translations.literal: The hawks and hounds of the Five Prefectures, following the Yuanhe precedent, were all released except for a measured number kept for palace hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Following Yuanhe precedent, the hawks and hunting dogs of the Five Prefectures were set free except for a limited number kept for palace hunts.

sentences.zh: 有司供宮禁年支物，並准貞元故事。

translations.literal: The annual supplies furnished by the responsible offices for the palace, all followed the Zhenyuan precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Annual provisions for the palace were scaled back to the levels of the Zhenyuan era.

sentences.zh: 省教坊、翰林、總監冗食千二百餘員，停諸司新加衣糧。

translations.literal: He reduced more than twelve hundred redundant sinecures in the Music Bureau, the Hanlin Academy, and the Directorate, and halted the newly added clothing and grain allotments of the various offices.
translations.idiomatic: He cut more than twelve hundred superfluous posts in the Music Bureau, the Hanlin Academy, and the Directorate, and stopped the new clothing and grain allowances that various offices had added.

sentences.zh: 御馬坊場及近歲別貯錢穀所佔陂田，悉歸之有司。

translations.literal: The dam lands occupied by the imperial horse pastures and by the grain and cash stored in recent years were all returned to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Flood-retention lands seized for imperial horse farms and for recent grain and cash hoards were all returned to the civil administration.

sentences.zh: 先宣索組繡、雕鏤之物，悉罷之。

translations.literal: Embroidered and carved luxuries previously ordered on imperial demand were all stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Orders for embroidered silks and carved ornaments were canceled outright.

sentences.zh: 敬宗之世，每月視朝不過一二，上始復舊制，每奇日未嘗不視朝，對宰相群臣延訪政事，久之方罷。

translations.literal: In Jingzong's time the emperor held court no more than once or twice a month; [Wenzong] now restored the old system, and on every odd-numbered day he never failed to hold court, questioning the chief ministers and the officials at length on government affairs before dismissing them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingzong the throne had been attended only once or twice a month. Wenzong restored the old practice: on every odd-numbered day he held court without fail, questioning chief ministers and officials at length on policy before adjourning.

sentences.zh: 待制官舊雖設之，未嘗召對，至是屢蒙延問。

translations.literal: The office of attendant-at-court had long existed but had never been summoned for consultation; from this time on [such officials] were repeatedly questioned at length.
translations.idiomatic: The post of attendant-at-court had existed for years but had never been called in for audience; now such men were questioned again and again.

sentences.zh: 其輟朝、放朝皆用偶日，中外翕然相賀，以為太平可冀。

translations.literal: Court recesses and dismissals all used even-numbered days; inside and outside the court rejoiced together, thinking that peace could be hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: Recesses and dismissals were scheduled only on even-numbered days. Court and country alike celebrated, believing that order might yet return.

sentences.zh: 文宗元聖昭獻孝皇帝上太和元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong, the Sagely, Cultured, Illustrious, and Filial—above, first year of Tahe (
translations.idiomatic: In the upper annals of Emperor Wenzong, the Sagely, Cultured, Illustrious, and Filial Emperor, the first year of Tahe (

sentences.zh: 丁未，公元八二七年）

translations.literal: dingwei, corresponding to AD 827)
translations.idiomatic: dingwei, AD 827)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，乙巳，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, in the second month, on the day yisi, [the emperor] pardoned all under Heaven and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the second month's yisi day, he proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 李同捷擅據滄景，朝廷經歲不問。

translations.literal: Li Tongjie had seized Cangzhou and Jingzhou on his own authority; for a full year the court did not press the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tongjie had seized Cangzhou and Jingzhou without authorization, and for a year the court left him alone.

sentences.zh: 同捷冀易世之後或加恩貸，三月，壬戌朔，遣掌書記崔從長奉表與其弟同志、同巽俱入見，請遵朝旨。

translations.literal: Tongjie hoped that after the change of reign he might receive clemency; in the third month, on the new moon of the day renxu, he sent his chief secretary Cui Congchang to present a memorial together with his younger brothers Tongzhi and Tongxun, all entering audience to request compliance with the court's command.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjie hoped a new reign might bring him mercy. On the third month's renxu new moon he sent his chief secretary Cui Congchang with memorial in hand, together with his brothers Tongzhi and Tongxun, all entering court to ask that he be allowed to obey imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 上雖虛懷聽納而不能堅決，與宰相議事已定，尋復中變。

translations.literal: Although the emperor was open-minded in listening and accepting, he could not be resolute; after he and the chief ministers had settled a matter, he would soon change his mind midway.
translations.idiomatic: Though willing to listen, the emperor could not hold a firm line: once he and his councilors had decided a policy, he would often reverse himself.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙辰，韋處厚於延英極論之，因請避位。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day bingchen, at Yanying Hall Wei Chuhou argued to the limit and thereupon asked to resign his post.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the fourth month's bingchen day, Wei Chuhou argued his case to the hilt in Yanying Hall and asked to step down.

sentences.zh: 上再三慰勞之。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him again and again and would not accept his resignation.

sentences.zh: 忠武節度使王沛薨。

translations.literal: Wang Pei, military commissioner of Zhongwu, died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pei, military commissioner of Zhongwu, died.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以太僕卿高瑀為忠武節度使。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen the Grand Master of the Imperial Stud Gao Yu was made military commissioner of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day Grand Master of the Imperial Stud Gao Yu was appointed military commissioner of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 自大歷以來，節度使多出禁軍，其禁軍大將資高者，皆以倍稱之息貸錢於富室，以賂中尉，動逾億萬，然後得之，未嘗由執政。

translations.literal: Since the Dali era most military commissioners had come from the Imperial Army; senior generals of the Imperial Army, the higher their standing, all borrowed money from wealthy houses at double-the-principal interest to bribe the grand marshals, often exceeding a hundred million, and only then obtained appointment—never through the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Dali era most frontier commissioners had been drawn from the Imperial Army. Senior generals borrowed from rich families at ruinous interest—often more than a hundred million cash—to bribe the eunuch grand marshals and buy their posts, never through the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，則重斂以償所負。

translations.literal: When they reached their commands they then levied heavily to repay what they owed.
translations.idiomatic: Once installed, they taxed their circuits mercilessly to pay their debts.

sentences.zh: 及沛薨，裴度、韋處厚始奏以瑀代之。

translations.literal: When Pei died, Pei Du and Wei Chuhou for the first time memorialized that Yu should replace him.
translations.idiomatic: After Pei's death Pei Du and Wei Chuhou memorialized for the first time that Gao Yu should succeed him.

sentences.zh: 中外相賀曰：「自今債帥鮮矣！

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court congratulated one another, saying: "From now on debt-commanders will be few!"
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike rejoiced, saying, "From now on there will be fewer debt-bought commanders!"

sentences.zh: 」五月，丙子，以天平節度使烏重胤為橫海節度使，以前橫海節度副使李同捷為兗海節度使。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month, on the day bingzi, Wu Chongyin, military commissioner of Tianping, was made military commissioner of Henghai, and the former vice commissioner of Henghai Li Tongjie was made military commissioner of Yanhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the bingzi day, Wu Chongyin of Tianping was transferred to Henghai, and Li Tongjie, former vice commissioner of Henghai, was named military commissioner of Yanhai.

sentences.zh: 朝廷猶慮河南、北節度使構扇同捷使拒命，乃加魏博史憲誠同平章事。

translations.literal: The court still feared that the military commissioners of Henan and Hebei might incite Tongjie to resist the command; thereupon Shi Xiancheng of Weibo was promoted to Jointly Appointed Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The court still worried that commissioners north and south of the Yellow River might stir Tongjie to defiance, and so promoted Shi Xiancheng of Weibo to Jointly Appointed Councilor.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，加盧龍李載義、平盧康志睦、成德王庭湊檢校官。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou Li Zaiyi of Lulong, Kang Zhimu of Pinglu, and Wang Tingcou of Chengde were given honorary chief-ministerial titles.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day Li Zaiyi of Lulong, Kang Zhimu of Pinglu, and Wang Tingcou of Chengde were granted honorary chief-ministerial titles.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵使王播自淮南入朝，力圖大用，所獻銀器以千計，綾絹以十萬計。

translations.literal: Wang Bo, commissioner of salt and iron, entered court from Huainan and strove for great appointment; the silver vessels he presented numbered in the thousands, and the silk brocade in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Salt and Iron Commissioner Wang Bo came to court from Huainan bent on high office, presenting thousands of silver vessels and tens of thousands of bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸巳，以播為左僕射、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day guisi, Bo was made Left Vice President of the Department of State Affairs and Jointly Appointed Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the guisi day, Wang Bo was made Left Vice President and Jointly Appointed Councilor.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸酉，葬睿武昭愍孝皇帝於莊陵，廟號敬宗。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day guiyou, the Sagely Martial, Illustrious, Lamented, and Filial Emperor was buried at Zhuang Mausoleum; his temple name was Jingzong.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the seventh month's guiyou day, Emperor Jingzong was buried at Zhuang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 李同捷托為將士所留，不受詔。

translations.literal: Li Tongjie pleaded that the officers and soldiers had detained him and would not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tongjie claimed his troops would not let him leave and refused to accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，武寧節度使王智興奏請將本軍三萬人，自備五月糧以討同捷，許之。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou Wang Zhixing, military commissioner of Wuning, memorialized requesting to lead thirty thousand men of his army, providing five months' provisions himself, to attack Tongjie; [the court] approved it.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day Wang Zhixing of Wuning asked to lead thirty thousand of his own troops, at his own expense for five months' rations, against Tongjie, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚子，削同捷官爵，命烏重胤、王智興、康志睦、史憲誠、李載義與義成節度使李聽、義武節度使張播各帥本軍討之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day gengzi, Tongjie's titles were stripped; Wu Chongyin, Wang Zhixing, Kang Zhimu, Shi Xiancheng, and Li Zaiyi, together with Li Ting, military commissioner of Yicheng, and Zhang Bo, military commissioner of Yiwu, were each ordered to lead their own armies to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the gengzi day, Tongjie was stripped of rank. Wu Chongyin, Wang Zhixing, Kang Zhimu, Shi Xiancheng, and Li Zaiyi, with Li Ting of Yicheng and Zhang Bo of Yiwu, were each ordered to march with their own forces against him.

sentences.zh: 同捷遣其子弟以珍玩、女妓賂河北諸鎮，戊午，李載義執其侄，並所賂獻之。

translations.literal: Tongjie sent his sons and younger kinsmen with precious objects and female entertainers to bribe the Hebei commands; on the day wuwu Li Zaiyi seized his nephew and presented him together with the bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjie sent relatives bearing treasures and courtesans to buy off the Hebei commissioners. On the wuwu day Li Zaiyi arrested his nephew and forwarded him to court together with the gifts.

sentences.zh: 史憲誠與李全略為婚姻，及同捷叛，密以糧助之。

translations.literal: Shi Xiancheng was related by marriage to Li Quanlue; when Tongjie rebelled he secretly sent him grain.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiancheng was tied to Li Quanlue by marriage, and when Tongjie rebelled he secretly supplied him with grain.

sentences.zh: 裴度不知其所為，謂憲誠無貳心。

translations.literal: Pei Du did not know what he was doing and said that Xiancheng had no disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du knew nothing of this and assured the throne that Xiancheng remained loyal.

sentences.zh: 憲誠遣親吏至中書請事，韋處厚謂曰：「晉公於上前以百口保爾使主，處厚則不然，但仰俟所為，自有朝典耳！
