translations.literal: Xiancheng sent a trusted clerk to the Secretariat to consult on affairs; Wei Chuhou said to him: "The Duke of Jin pledged before the emperor a hundred lives for your commissioner; I am not the same—I simply await your commissioner's conduct, and the court's statutes will take their course!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng sent a trusted clerk to the Secretariat for guidance. Wei Chuhou told him, "The Duke of Jin staked a hundred lives before the throne on your master's loyalty. I make no such pledge. I will simply watch what your master does, and the law will do the rest."

sentences.zh: 」憲誠懼，不敢復與同捷通。

translations.literal: " Xiancheng was afraid and dared not communicate with Tongjie again.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng was terrified and dared not traffic with Tongjie again.

sentences.zh: 王庭湊為同捷求節鉞不獲，乃助之為亂，出兵境上以撓魏師。

translations.literal: Wang Tingcou, having sought a commission for Tongjie without obtaining it, then helped him in rebellion and sent troops beyond his borders to harass the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingcou, denied a commission for Tongjie, aided his revolt and sent troops across the border to harry the Wei expedition.

sentences.zh: 又遣使厚賂沙陀酋長朱邪執宜，欲與之連兵，執宜拒不受。

translations.literal: He also sent an envoy with rich bribes to the Shatuo chieftain Zhuye Zhiyi, wishing to join forces with him; Zhiyi refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys laden with gifts to the Shatuo chief Zhuye Zhiyi, hoping for an alliance; Zhiyi refused them.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，天平、橫海節度使烏重胤擊同捷，屢破之。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, Wu Chongyin, military commissioner of Tianping and Henghai, attacked Tongjie and repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Wu Chongyin of Tianping and Henghai attacked Tongjie and beat him again and again.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙寅，重胤薨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day bingyin, Chongyin died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the bingyin day, Wu Chongyin died.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以保義節度使李寰為橫海節度使，從王智興之請也。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen Li Huan, military commissioner of Baoyi, was made military commissioner of Henghai, in accordance with Wang Zhixing's request.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day Li Huan of Baoyi was transferred to Henghai at Wang Zhixing's request.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚戌，加王智興同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day gengxu, Wang Zhixing was promoted to Jointly Appointed Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the gengxu day, Wang Zhixing was made Jointly Appointed Councilor.

sentences.zh: 文宗元聖昭獻孝皇帝上太和二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong, the Sagely, Cultured, Illustrious, and Filial—above, second year of Tahe (
translations.idiomatic: In the upper annals of Emperor Wenzong, the Sagely, Cultured, Illustrious, and Filial Emperor, the second year of Tahe (

sentences.zh: 戌申，公元八二八年）

translations.literal: wushen, corresponding to AD 828)
translations.idiomatic: wushen, AD 828)

sentences.zh: 春，三月，己卯，王智興攻棣州，焚其三門。

translations.literal: In spring, in the third month, on the day jimao, Wang Zhixing attacked De Prefecture and burned its three gate towers.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the third month's jimao day, Wang Zhixing attacked De Prefecture and burned its three gate towers.

sentences.zh: 自元和之末，宦官益橫，建置天子在其掌握，威權出人主之右，人莫敢言。

translations.literal: From the end of the Yuanhe era the eunuchs grew ever more overbearing; they installed and removed emperors at their grasp, and their authority and power stood to the right of the sovereign—no one dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Since the close of the Yuanhe era the eunuchs had grown ever bolder, enthroning and deposing emperors at will. Their power eclipsed the throne itself, and no one dared protest.

sentences.zh: 辛已，上親策制舉人，賢良方正，昌平劉蕡對策極言其禍，其略曰：「陛下宜先憂者：宮闈將變，社稷將危，天下將傾，海內將亂。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi the emperor personally examined the civil-service candidates of the special decree examination for "upright and good," and Liu Zhen of Changping answered the policy question by speaking bluntly of the disaster; in summary he said: "What Your Majesty should worry about first: the inner palace is about to change, the altars of state are about to be endangered, the realm is about to topple, and within the seas disorder is about to break out.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day the emperor held the special civil examination for "upright and good" candidates. Liu Zhen of Changping answered with a memorial that laid bare the peril in the plainest terms: "Your Majesty's first concerns ought to be these: the inner palace is on the verge of upheaval, the altars of state are in danger, the realm is tottering, and turmoil is about to engulf the empire.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：』陛下將杜篡弒之漸，則居正位而近正人，遠刀鋸之賤，親骨鯁之直，輔相得以專其任，庶職得以守其官，奈何以褻近五六人總天下大政！

translations.literal: " He also said: "If Your Majesty wishes to cut off the gradual growth of usurpation and regicide, then occupy the correct position and keep upright men near, keep far from the base of the knife and saw, be close to blunt, loyal remonstrators, let the chief ministers fully carry out their duties, and let the hundred offices keep to their posts—how can you let five or six lewd intimates hold all great government of the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "To choke off the drift toward regicide, hold the throne in dignity and keep honest men close. Banish the butcher's minions; cherish the blunt counselors who speak truth. Let your chief ministers govern, and let every office do its work—how can five or six favored eunuchs run the empire?"

sentences.zh: 禍稔蕭牆，奸生帷幄，臣恐曹節、侯覽復生於今日。

translations.literal: "Disaster ripens within the palace walls; treachery is born inside the curtain. I fear Cao Jie and Hou Lan are being reborn in our own day."
translations.idiomatic: "Disaster is ripening behind the palace walls; treachery is breeding within the curtained hall. I fear that Cao Jie and Hou Lan live again in our time."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「忠賢無腹心之寄，閫寺恃廢立之權，陷先君不得正其終，致陛下不得正其始。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Loyal ministers have no place to lodge their hearts; the eunuch commanders rely on the power to depose and establish [emperors]. They trapped the late emperor so that he could not end his reign properly, and they have caused Your Majesty not to begin yours properly."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Loyal ministers have nowhere to place their trust. The eunuch commanders rest on the power to make and unmake emperors. They prevented your predecessor from ending his reign in peace, and they have kept you from beginning yours in legitimacy."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「威柄陵夷，籓臣跋扈。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Imperial authority declines day by day; the frontier lords are arrogant and domineering."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Sovereign power erodes daily, while the military commissioners grow insolent on their borders."

sentences.zh: 或有不達人臣之節，首亂者以安君為名；

translations.literal: Some who do not understand a subject's propriety take the lead in disorder in the name of securing the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: Some who lack a subject's restraint raise rebellion in the name of saving the throne;

sentences.zh: 不究《春秋》之微，稱兵者以逐惡為義。

translations.literal: without probing the subtle meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, those who take up arms claim the righteousness of driving out evil.
translations.idiomatic: without grasping the Spring and Autumn Annals' deeper lesson, men who march armies call it righteous to expel the wicked.

sentences.zh: 則政刑不由乎天子，征伐必自於諸侯。

translations.literal: Then government and punishments no longer proceed from the Son of Heaven, and campaigns and punishments necessarily originate with the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Then law and punishment no longer flow from the Son of Heaven, and war is waged only at the command of the regional lords.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「陛下何不塞陰邪之路，屏褻狎之臣，制侵陵迫脅之心，復門戶掃除之役，戒其所宜戒，憂其所宜憂！

translations.literal: " He also said: "Why does Your Majesty not block the path of hidden evil, dismiss lewd and familiar ministers, restrain hearts that encroach and coerce, restore the work of guarding the gates and sweeping the court—warn where warning is due, and worry where worry is due!"
translations.idiomatic: He urged: "Block the road of secret malice. Cast out the emperor's coarse intimates. Curb the impulse to bully and threaten. Restore the old duties of gatekeeping and court order. Warn yourself where warning is needed; fear what ought to be feared."

sentences.zh: 既不能治於前，當治於後，既不能正其始，當正其終；

translations.literal: If you could not govern what came before, govern what comes after; if you could not set right the beginning, set right the end;
translations.idiomatic: If you could not set things right at the start, set them right at the finish; if you could not cure what came before, cure what comes after.

sentences.zh: 則可以虔奉典謨，克承丕構矣。

translations.literal: then you may reverently follow the canonical models and succeed to the great foundation."
translations.idiomatic: Then you may reverently uphold the classics and inherit the great enterprise of your house."

sentences.zh: 昔秦之亡也失於強暴，漢之亡也失於微弱。

translations.literal: In antiquity Qin perished through excess violence; Han perished through excess weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Qin fell because its rule was too brutal; Han fell because its rule was too feeble.

sentences.zh: 強暴則賊臣畏死而害上，微弱則奸臣竊權而震主。

translations.literal: When violent, treacherous ministers fear death and harm their sovereign; when weak, crafty ministers steal power and shake the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Under brutal rule, treacherous ministers, fearing for their lives, murder their lord; under feeble rule, crafty ministers seize power and terrify the throne.

sentences.zh: 伏見敬宗皇帝不虞亡秦之禍，不翦其萌。

translations.literal: I observe that Emperor Jingzong did not guard against Qin's manner of perishing and did not cut off the evil at its sprout.
translations.idiomatic: I see that Emperor Jingzong never foresaw Qin's fate and never cut the evil in its bud.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下深軫亡漢之憂，以杜其漸，則祖宗之鴻業可紹，三、五之遐軌可追矣。

translations.literal: I pray that Your Majesty will deeply take to heart Han's manner of perishing and cut off the gradual growth of evil; then the magnificent enterprise of the ancestors may be continued, and the distant model of the Three Dynasties may be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty will take Han's fall deeply to heart and stop the rot while it is still slight. Then the ancestral legacy may be renewed and the distant example of the sage kings pursued once more.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「臣聞昔漢元帝即位之初，更制七十餘事，其心甚誠，其稱甚美，然而紀綱日紊，國祚日衰，奸宄日強，黎元日困者，以其不能擇賢明而任之，失其操柄也。

translations.literal: " He also said: "I have heard that when Emperor Yuan of Han first took the throne he changed more than seventy institutions; his heart was very sincere and his reputation very fine—yet day by day the statutes grew disorderly, day by day the fortune of the state declined, day by day treachery grew strong, and day by day the common people were distressed, because he could not choose the worthy and enlightened and employ them, and lost hold of the helm."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "When Emperor Yuan of Han first reigned he reformed more than seventy institutions. His intent was sincere and his praise resounded—yet order unraveled daily, the dynasty weakened daily, villains grew bolder daily, and the people suffered daily, because he could not choose wise men and give them real authority. He lost the tiller of state."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「陛下誠能揭國權以歸相，持兵柄以歸將，則心無不達，行無不孚矣。

translations.literal: " He also said: "If Your Majesty can truly raise the authority of the state and return it to the chief ministers, and hold the military power and return it to the generals, then no thought will go unheeded and no act will fail to win trust."
translations.idiomatic: He said further: "If Your Majesty will truly restore civil authority to the chief ministers and military authority to the generals, nothing you intend will go unheard and nothing you do will lack credibility."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「法宜畫一，官宜正名。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The law ought to be uniform; offices ought to have correct names."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Law should be one; offices should bear their proper names."

sentences.zh: 今分外官、中官之員，立南司、北司之局，或犯禁於南則亡命於北，或正刑於外則破律於中，法出多門，人無所措，實由兵農勢異而中外法殊也。

translations.literal: Now the posts of outer officials and inner officials are set up separately, and the bureaus of the southern and northern administrations are established; if one violates prohibition in the south he flees to the north, if one is punished by regular law outside he breaks the statutes within—law issues from many gates and people have nowhere to turn; this truly comes from the differing power of soldiers and farmers and the differing law inside and outside."
translations.idiomatic: "Today outer and inner officials multiply without limit; southern and northern bureaus stand side by side. Break the law in one jurisdiction and flee to the other; punish a crime in the open court and see it voided within the palace. When law has many mouths, the people do not know where to stand. This comes of treating army and empire as separate worlds, with one law for the court and another for the realm."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：』今夏官不知兵籍，止於奉朝請；

translations.literal: " He also said: "This summer the Ministry of War does not know the military registers and is limited to attendance at court;"
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "Today the Ministry of War no longer knows the rolls of the armies and exists only to attend morning audience;

sentences.zh: 六軍不主兵事，止於養勳階。

translations.literal: The Six Armies do not command military affairs but only cultivate ranks of merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Armies no longer commanded military affairs but only cultivated ranks of merit.

sentences.zh: 軍容合中官之政，戎律附內臣之職。

translations.literal: Military prestige merged with the policies of inner officials; martial law attached to the duties of palace servants.
translations.idiomatic: Military prestige merged with eunuch policy, and martial law became an inner-court function.

sentences.zh: 首一戴武弁，疾文吏如仇讎。

translations.literal: Once they donned the warrior's cap, they hated civil officials like mortal enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Once they donned the warrior's cap, they hated civil officials like mortal enemies.

sentences.zh: 足一蹈軍門，視農夫如草芥。

translations.literal: Once they set foot in the army gate, they regarded farmers as worthless weeds.
translations.idiomatic: Once they entered the army gate, they treated farmers as worthless weeds.

sentences.zh: 謀不足以翦除凶逆，而詐足以抑揚威福；

translations.literal: Their plotting was insufficient to cut down the vicious and rebellious, yet their deceit was enough to raise and lower power and favor;
translations.idiomatic: They lacked the wit to destroy traitors, yet their cunning sufficed to raise and lower power and favor;

sentences.zh: 勇不足以鎮衛社稷，而暴足以侵軼里閭。

translations.literal: their courage was insufficient to guard the altars of state, yet their violence was enough to trample villages and lanes.
translations.idiomatic: their courage could not guard the realm, yet their violence could trample villages and lanes.

sentences.zh: 羈紲籓臣，干陵宰舖，隳裂王度，汩亂朝經。

translations.literal: They bound frontier ministers, overawed chief ministers, shattered royal standards, and muddied court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: They bound frontier ministers, overawed chief ministers, shattered royal standards, and muddied court regulations.

sentences.zh: 張武夫之威，上以制君父；

translations.literal: They stretched the might of warriors upward to control father and sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: They stretched warriors' might upward to control emperor and father;

sentences.zh: 假天子之命，下以御英豪。

translations.literal: they borrowed the Son of Heaven's mandate downward to command heroes and champions.
translations.idiomatic: they borrowed the Son of Heaven's mandate downward to command heroes and champions.

sentences.zh: 有藏奸觀釁之父，無伏節死難之義。

translations.literal: There were fathers who hid treachery and watched for openings, but no righteousness of laying down one's life in loyal death.
translations.idiomatic: There were fathers who hid treachery and watched for openings, but none who died loyal deaths for the throne.

sentences.zh: 豈先王經文緯武之旨邪！

translations.literal: How could this be the intent of the former kings who wove culture and martial power together!
translations.idiomatic: How could this be what the former kings intended when they wove culture and arms together!

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「臣非不知言發而禍應，計行而身戮，蓋痛社稷之危，哀生人之困，豈忍姑息時忌，竊陛下一命之寵哉！

translations.literal: He also said: 'Your servant is not unaware that words once spoken bring calamity in answer, and plans once carried out bring the body to execution — yet I grieve the altars of state in peril and pity the people's distress; how could I bear to indulge the taboos of the time and steal Your Majesty's single favor of office!'
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, 'I know that words bring calamity and action brings death — yet I grieve the realm's peril and pity the people's distress. How could I indulge the taboos of the age and steal Your Majesty's favor!'

sentences.zh: 閏月，丙戌朔，史憲誠奏遣其子副大使唐、都知兵馬使亓志紹將兵二萬五千趣德州討李同捷。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the first day bingxu, Shi Xiancheng memorialized dispatching his son, Vice Ambassador Tang, and Army Cavalry Commissioner Qi Zhishao to lead twenty-five thousand troops toward Dezhou to attack Li Tongjie.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the bingxu new-moon day, Shi Xiancheng reported sending his son Tang and Cavalry Commissioner Qi Zhishao with twenty-five thousand troops toward Dezhou against Li Tongjie.

sentences.zh: 時憲誠欲助同捷，唐泣諫，且請發兵討之；

translations.literal: At that time Xiancheng wished to aid Tongjie; Tang remonstrated through tears and also asked to raise troops to attack him;
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng wished to aid Tongjie, but Tang remonstrated through tears and asked to raise troops against him;

sentences.zh: 憲誠不能違。

translations.literal: Xiancheng could not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 甲午，賢良方正裴休、李郃、李甘、杜牧、馬植、崔璵、王式、崔慎由等二十二人中第，皆除官。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, the Worthy and Upright candidates Pei Xiu, Li He, Li Gan, Du Mu, Ma Zhi, Cui Yu, Wang Shi, Cui Shenyou, and twenty-two others in all passed the examination and were all given offices.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day Worthy and Upright candidates Pei Xiu, Li He, Li Gan, Du Mu, Ma Zhi, Cui Yu, Wang Shi, Cui Shenyou, and twenty-two others passed the examination and received offices.

sentences.zh: 考官左散騎常侍馮宿等見劉蕡策，皆歎服，而畏宦官，不敢取。

translations.literal: Examining officials including Left Regular Attendant Feng Su saw Liu Fen's examination answer and all sighed in admiration, yet feared the eunuchs and dared not pass him.
translations.idiomatic: Examining officials including Left Regular Attendant Feng Su read Liu Fen's answer and admired it, yet feared the eunuchs and dared not pass him.

sentences.zh: 詔下，物論囂然稱屈。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, public opinion loudly cried injustice.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, public opinion loudly cried injustice.

sentences.zh: 諫官、御史欲論奏，執政抑之。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials and censors wished to memorialize on it; the chief ministers suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials and censors wished to protest, but the chief ministers suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 李郃曰：「劉蕡下第，我輩登科，能無厚顏！

translations.literal: Li He said: 'Liu Fen failed the examination while we passed — can we not feel shame!'
translations.idiomatic: Li He said, 'Liu Fen failed while we passed — how can we not feel shame!'

sentences.zh: 」乃上疏，以為：「蕡所對策，漢、魏以來無與為比。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial, stating: 'Fen's examination answer has had no equal since Han and Wei.'
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial stating that Fen's answer had had no equal since Han and Wei.

sentences.zh: 今有司以蕡指切左右，不敢以聞，恐中良道窮，綱紀遂絕。

translations.literal: 'Now the authorities, because Fen sharply criticized those close to the throne, dare not report it — I fear the upright path will be cut off and regulation and law will perish.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Now the authorities, because Fen criticized the emperor's intimates, dare not report it — I fear the upright path will be cut off and law will perish.'

sentences.zh: 況臣所對不及蕡遠甚，乞回臣所授以旌蕡直。

translations.literal: 'Moreover, your servant's answer falls far short of Fen's; I beg to return what was granted me to honor Fen's integrity.'
translations.idiomatic: 'My own answer falls far short of Fen's; I beg to return my appointment to honor his integrity.'

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: There was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: There was no reply.

sentences.zh: 蕡由是不得仁於朝，終於使府御史。

translations.literal: Fen thereby failed to find favor at court and ended as a censor in a military commissioner's office.
translations.idiomatic: Fen never found favor at court and ended his career as a censor in a military governor's staff.

sentences.zh: 牧，佑之孫；

translations.literal: Mu was the grandson of [Du] You;
translations.idiomatic: Du Mu was Du You's grandson;

sentences.zh: 植，勳之子；

translations.literal: Zhi was the son of [Ma] Xun;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhi was Ma Xun's son;

sentences.zh: 式，起之子；

translations.literal: Shi was the son of [Wang] Qi;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shi was Wang Qi's son;

sentences.zh: 慎由，融之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Shenyou was the great-great-grandson of [Cui] Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shenyou was Cui Rong's great-great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，晉王普薨。

translations.literal: In summer, in the sixth month, Prince of Jin Pu died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the sixth month, Prince of Jin Pu died.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，贈悼懷太子。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, he was posthumously honored as the Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day he was posthumously honored as the Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭太后幼去鄉里，有弟一人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Empress Dowager Xiao was young she left her native place and had one younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: When young, Empress Dowager Xiao left her native place; she had one younger brother.

sentences.zh: 上即位，命福建觀察使求訪，莫知所在。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, he ordered the Fujian observation commissioner to seek him, but no one knew where he was.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascended the throne he ordered the Fujian observation commissioner to seek him, but no one knew where he was.

sentences.zh: 有茶綱役人蕭洪，自言有姊流落，商人趙縝引之見太后近親呂璋之妻，亦不能辨，與之俱見太后。

translations.literal: A tea-transport laborer named Xiao Hong said he had a sister who had been lost; the merchant Zhao Zhen led him to meet the wife of the empress dowager's close kinsman Lü Zhang, who also could not identify him, and together they were brought before the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: A tea-transport laborer named Xiao Hong claimed a lost sister; merchant Zhao Zhen brought him to the wife of the empress dowager's kinsman Lü Zhang, who could not identify him, and they were brought before the empress dowager together.

sentences.zh: 上以為得真舅，甲子，以為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: The emperor believed he had found the true maternal uncle; on the day jiazi he was appointed crown prince's study companion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed he had found his true uncle; on the jiazi day Hong was appointed crown prince's study companion.

sentences.zh: 峰州刺史王升朝叛。

translations.literal: Fengzhou Prefect Wang Shengchao rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Fengzhou Prefect Wang Shengchao rebelled.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，安南都護武陵韓約討斬之。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Protector-General of Annan Han Yue of Wuling attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day Protector-General of Annan Han Yue of Wuling attacked and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 王庭湊陰以兵及鹽糧助李同捷，上欲討之。

translations.literal: Wang Tingcou secretly sent troops and salt grain to aid Li Tongjie; the emperor wished to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingcou secretly sent troops and salt grain to aid Li Tongjie, and the emperor wished to attack him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲辰，詔中書集百官議其事。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day jiachen, an edict ordered the Secretariat to gather the hundred officials to deliberate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the seventh month's jiachen day, an edict ordered the Secretariat to gather officials to deliberate the matter.

sentences.zh: 宰相以下莫敢違，衛尉卿殷侑獨以為：「廷湊雖附兇徒，事未甚露，宜且含容，專討同捷。

translations.literal: From the chief ministers down none dared dissent; only Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia Yin You held: 'Although Tingcou has attached himself to vicious rebels, the matter is not yet very exposed; he should for the moment be tolerated while we concentrate on attacking Tongjie.'
translations.idiomatic: From the chief ministers down none dared dissent; only Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia Yin You argued that although Tingcou had aided rebels, the matter was not yet clear and he should be tolerated while the court concentrated on Tongjie.

sentences.zh: 」己巳，下詔罪狀廷湊，命鄰道各嚴兵守備，聽其自新。

translations.literal: On the day jisi an edict was issued listing Tingcou's crimes and ordering neighboring circuits each to ready troops on guard, allowing him to reform himself.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day an edict listed Tingcou's crimes and ordered neighboring circuits to ready their defenses while allowing him to reform.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁亥，王智興奏拔棣州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day dinghai, Wang Zhixing reported capturing Di Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the dinghai day, Wang Zhixing reported capturing Di Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李寰自晉州兵赴鎮，不戢士卒，所過殘暴，至則擁兵不進，但坐索供饋。

translations.literal: Li Huan marched troops from Jin Prefecture to his command, did not restrain his soldiers, and wherever they passed they were cruel and violent; on arrival he held his troops back from advancing and merely sat demanding supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan marched troops from Jin Prefecture to his post without restraining them; they ravaged the countryside, and on arrival he held back from battle and merely demanded supplies.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以寰為夏綏節度使。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, Huan was appointed military governor of Xiasui.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day Huan was appointed military governor of Xiasui.

sentences.zh: 甲午，詔削奪王庭湊官爵，命諸軍四面進討。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, an edict stripped Wang Tingcou of office and rank and ordered armies on all sides to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day an edict stripped Wang Tingcou of office and rank and ordered armies on all sides to attack.

sentences.zh: 加王智興守司徒，以前夏綏節度使傅良弼為橫海節度使。

translations.literal: Wang Zhixing was promoted to acting Minister of Education; former Xiasui Military Governor Fu Liangbi was made military governor of Henghai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhixing was promoted to acting Minister of Education; former Xiasui Military Governor Fu Liangbi was made military governor of Henghai.

sentences.zh: 岳王緄薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Chun died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yue Chun died.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，容管奏安南軍亂，逐都護韓約。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, Rong Circuit reported that the Annan army had mutinied and driven out Protector-General Han Yue.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day Rong Circuit reported that the Annan army had mutinied and driven out Protector-General Han Yue.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，洋王忻薨。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, Prince of Yang Xin died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Prince of Yang Xin died.

sentences.zh: 魏博敗橫海兵於平原，遂拔之。

translations.literal: Weibo defeated Henghai troops at Pingyuan and then captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo defeated Henghai troops at Pingyuan and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸未朔，易定節度使柳公濟奏攻李同捷堅固寨，拔之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day guiwei, Yiding Military Governor Liu Gongji reported attacking Li Tongjie's Jian'gu stockade and capturing it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the guiwei new-moon day, Yiding Military Governor Liu Gongji reported capturing Li Tongjie's Jian'gu stockade.

sentences.zh: 又破其兵於寨東。

translations.literal: He also defeated Tongjie's troops east of the stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated Tongjie's troops east of the stockade.

sentences.zh: 時河南、北諸軍討同捷久未成功，每有小勝，則虛張首虜以邀厚賞，朝廷竭力奉之，江、淮為之耗弊。

translations.literal: At that time the armies of Henan and Hebei campaigning against Tongjie had long failed to succeed; whenever there was a small victory they falsely magnified heads and captives to seek rich rewards, and the court strained to supply them until the Yangzi and Huai regions were drained and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan and Hebei armies had long failed against Tongjie; after every small victory they inflated reports of captives to claim rich rewards, draining the court until the Yangzi and Huai regions were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 傅良弼至陝而薨。

translations.literal: Fu Liangbi reached Shan Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liangbi reached Shan Prefecture and died.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以左金吾大將軍李祐為橫海節度使。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, Left Golden Crow Grand General Li You was appointed military governor of Henghai.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day Left Golden Crow Grand General Li You was appointed military governor of Henghai.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，禁中昭德寺火，延及宮人所居，燒死者數百人。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, fire broke out at Zhaode Temple within the Forbidden City and spread to where palace women lived; several hundred who burned died.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day fire broke out at Zhaode Temple in the palace and spread to the women's quarters; several hundred died in the flames.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁已，王智興奏兵馬使李君謀將兵濟河，破無棣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day dingsi, Wang Zhixing reported that Cavalry Commissioner Li Junmou led troops across the river and broke Wudi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the dingsi day, Wang Zhixing reported that Cavalry Commissioner Li Junmou crossed the river and captured Wudi.

sentences.zh: 壬申，中書侍郎、同平章事韋處厚薨。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister Wei Chuhou died.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day Vice Director Wei Chuhou died.

sentences.zh: 李同捷軍勢日蹙，王庭湊不能救，乃遣人說魏博大將亓志紹使殺史憲誠父子取魏博。

translations.literal: Li Tongjie's military situation grew daily tighter; Wang Tingcou could not rescue him and therefore sent men to persuade Weibo Grand General Qi Zhishao to kill Shi Xiancheng and his son and seize Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tongjie's position grew daily tighter; Wang Tingcou could not save him and sent men to persuade Weibo Grand General Qi Zhishao to kill Shi Xiancheng and his son and seize Weibo.

sentences.zh: 志紹遂作亂，引所部兵二萬人還逼魏州。

translations.literal: Zhishao thereupon raised a disturbance, leading twenty thousand troops of his command back to press on Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishao thereupon rebelled, leading twenty thousand troops back to threaten Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，命諫議大夫柏耆宣慰魏博，且發義成、河陽兵以討志紹。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, Remonstrance Official Bai Qi was ordered to console Weibo and also to raise troops from Yicheng and Heyang to attack Zhishao.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day Remonstrance Official Bai Qi was sent to console Weibo and to raise troops from Yicheng and Heyang against Zhishao.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以翰林學士路隋為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, Hanlin Academician Lu Sui was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day Hanlin Academician Lu Sui was made Vice Director and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 辛已，史憲誠奏亓志紹兵屯永濟，告急求援。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, Shi Xiancheng reported that Qi Zhishao's troops were encamped at Yongji and urgently sought aid.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day Shi Xiancheng reported that Qi Zhishao's troops were at Yongji and urgently sought aid.

sentences.zh: 詔義成節度使李聽帥滄州行營諸軍以討志紹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yicheng Military Governor Li Ting to command the Cangzhou field armies to attack Zhishao.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yicheng Military Governor Li Ting to command the Cangzhou field armies against Zhishao.
